item.title: Wisconsin vs. Iowa series history ahead of 100th all-time meeting
item.description: Officially, this is set to be the 100th all-time meeting between the Wisconsin Badgers and Iowa Hawkeyes . There's nothing quite like rivalry week, and while the Battle for the Heartland Trophy hasn't gone the Badgers ' way in a few years, that should only add more fuel to the fire. Iowa dominated UW last season, 37-0. Badgers fans will remember that it came in a six-game stretch in which they scored a combined 41 points from Sept. 13 to Oct. 25. The Hawkeyes have been in possession of the trophy since 2022. Wisconsin hasn't beaten Iowa since Oct. 30, 2021, when they took care of business 27-7 in Madison. UW's last win in Iowa City was on Sept. 22, 2018, so it's been eight years since the Badgers have gone to Kinnick Stadium and taken care of business. Wisconsin barely leads the all-time series vs. Iowa All-time, Wisconsin is 49-48-2 against Iowa. The Badgers are just 20-27-1 on the road, so that's certainly something to monitor ahead of their Big Noon Kickoff on Halloween. This current four-game skid is tied for the second longest, but it's nowhere near as bad as when Iowa won 10 straight from 1985 to 1996. A 10-10 tie in 1984 helped lessen the blow as Iowa had also won seven in a row from 1977 to 1983. When was the first ever meeting? UW took care of business in the first-ever meeting between these two teams, 44-0, on Oct. 29, 1894. They wouldn't meet again until 1906, but it's worth noting that Wisconsin won its first six games against Iowa. item.title: Fatal Frame Transforms an Ordinary Hobby Into Bone-Chilling Horror
item.description: Fatal Frame creator and director Makoto Shibata once said that the most frightening thing is people's imaginations, which are populated by monsters that we can't see. When designing the first installment of one of the 2000s' most iconic horror series, his desire was to create a game that would make players feel terrified by the mere idea of even grabbing the controller. But the way he got there was unconventional: by making players take photos of ghosts.

item.title: AI has come for Arizona’s water
item.description: A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one building, and then another, and then the ground opens up where construction crews have dug up the earth so a third building can rise. There is a parking lot, and then another, and then another. There is an empty lot on the other side of the street, full of cars and the occasional food truck to feed the thousands of laborers who are busy transforming this expanse of desert into an industrial park. There is dust, so much of it, choking the air. I stand before the savior of Arizona’s economy. Like all great deities, it demands sacrifice. In the desert, nothing is more precious than water, and water is what must be given — nearly 5 million gallons a day, every day, sourced from Phoenix’s municipal supply. The offering has been well worth it. All of this is the fruit of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading producer of microchips. Its Arizona operation is the result of a pre-pandemic gamble Phoenix made to revive its sluggish economy , which never quite rebounded from the Great Recession. Now TSMC’s foundry looms over the city’s outskirts. TSMC is a success story, one that some local leaders may have hoped to repeat with hyperscale data center developments. The progression may have seemed natural: The Grand Canyon State is not only home to the largest chip factory this side of the Pacific but also 172 data centers , neither of which faced much pushback. But the newer, larger developments being proposed from Phoenix to Tucson demand more of everything — more water, more power, more land — than Arizonans are willing to give. Where TSMC was welcomed with open arms and the first wave of data centers was largely ignored, new developments are facing mass backlash in Arizona, where a grassroots, surprisingly bipartisan coalition of residents has united against data centers. Now the state has a sixth C, Arizona native Christine Mackay tells me. “Chips.” In reporting this story, I spoke to local activists and economic developers, elected officials and their angry constituents. I sat in on city council meetings where people lined up by the dozens to speak up against data center projects, and in cozy suburban homes where tight-knit groups of former strangers told me about the struggle that brought them together. I pored over maps of Arizona’s dry, cracked landscape with laypeople who, over the past two years, have made themselves experts on zoning and land use and water consumption so they can understand the beast they’re trying to fight. item.dc:creator: Gaby Del Valle
item.content:encoded: A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one building, and then another, and then the ground opens up where construction crews have dug up the earth so a third building can rise. There is a parking lot, and then another, and then another. There is an empty lot on the other side of the street, full of cars and the occasional food truck to feed the thousands of laborers who are busy transforming this expanse of desert into an industrial park. There is dust, so much of it, choking the air. I stand before the savior of Arizona’s economy. Like all great deities, it demands sacrifice. In the desert, nothing is more precious than water, and water is what must be given — nearly 5 million gallons a day, every day, sourced from Phoenix’s municipal supply. The offering has been well worth it. All of this is the fruit of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading producer of microchips. Its Arizona operation is the result of a pre-pandemic gamble Phoenix made to revive its sluggish economy , which never quite rebounded from the Great Recession. Now TSMC’s foundry looms over the city’s outskirts. TSMC is a success story, one that some local leaders may have hoped to repeat with hyperscale data center developments. The progression may have seemed natural: The Grand Canyon State is not only home to the largest chip factory this side of the Pacific but also 172 data centers , neither of which faced much pushback. But the newer, larger developments being proposed from Phoenix to Tucson demand more of everything — more water, more power, more land — than Arizonans are willing to give. Where TSMC was welcomed with open arms and the first wave of data centers was largely ignored, new developments are facing mass backlash in Arizona, where a grassroots, surprisingly bipartisan coalition of residents has united against data centers. Now the state has a sixth C, Arizona native Christine Mackay tells me. “Chips.” In reporting this story, I spoke to local activists and economic developers, elected officials and their angry constituents. I sat in on city council meetings where people lined up by the dozens to speak up against data center projects, and in cozy suburban homes where tight-knit groups of former strangers told me about the struggle that brought them together. I pored over maps of Arizona’s dry, cracked landscape with laypeople who, over the past two years, have made themselves experts on zoning and land use and water consumption so they can understand the beast they’re trying to fight. The locals on both sides of this debate claim to want the same thing: a better, more prosperous Arizona. Their visions for achieving it, however, are completely at odds. In Arizona and elsewhere, data center developers have tried to win over locals by making enticing promises about the jobs, tax revenue, and infrastructure they’ll bring with them. All they ask for in exchange is water — and, they swear, not nearly as much of it as you’d expect. Some hyperscale data centers, like Google’s facility in The Dalles, Oregon, use about 1.5 million gallons a day, about one-third of what TSMC’s Arizona complex consumes in the same timeframe. Those reassurances, however, aren’t enough to assuage Arizonans, who now have to contend with the fact that the state will soon lose access to nearly 30 percent of the water it receives from the Colorado River. Even now, as people across the country sour on AI and fight against data centers in their communities, TSMC’s Arizona operation hums along without significant opposition. And yet it’s impossible to make sense of why Arizonans are so opposed to new data center development without first understanding why they eagerly welcomed TSMC, even though both industries must contend with the issue that has plagued Arizona since its founding: There isn’t enough water. For as long as anyone could remember, business in Arizona revolved around the storied “five C’s”: cattle, copper, cotton, citrus, and climate, a catchall for the region’s mild, salubrious winters, which locals say often more than make up for the sweltering summers. Now the state has a sixth C, Arizona native Christine Mackay tells me. “Chips.” The TSMC development is, in a sense, Mackay’s doing. As the head of Phoenix’s economic development office, she spearheaded the effort that brought the Taiwanese giant to the Sonoran Desert. In 2020, while the global economy was all but shut down, TSMC made an announcement. The same forces that brought the world to a standstill had created even more demand for TSMC’s products, and in response, TSMC would be opening an advanced semiconductor foundry — a “fab,” in industry jargon — in Phoenix. Initially, TSMC predicted that it would pour $12 billion into Arizona’s economy by 2029. Since then, TSMC’s projected expenditure in the state has ballooned to $265 billion, what the company touts as the largest foreign direct investment in US history. TSMC just put the finishing touches on its second fab in a formerly desolate swath of north Phoenix, with a third under construction and plans for several more underway. This buildout has been more than a decade in the making. TSMC started shopping around for a US location in 2016. That year, Mackay said, the company put out a request for proposals through a codename. No one won. “We aren’t a group that takes no for an answer,” Mackay said proudly. Her office asked TSMC executives what they thought Arizona was missing, and then spent the next three years addressing their concerns. In 2019, Phoenix sent a delegation to Taiwan to share a new development plan for a science and technology park, the nucleus of which would be a factory, ideally one of TSMC’s fabs. “They agreed they needed to come back and take another look at Phoenix,” Mackay told me. Her team showed them two locations: Laveen, Arizona, a suburb southwest of Phoenix, and, just north of the city, an undeveloped area roughly the size of Manhattan called Biscuit Flats, so named, Mackay told me, because “it’s as round and flat as a biscuit.” “That very day,” she recalled, “they said, ‘This could work.’” What followed was a flurry of development unlike anything the state has ever seen. TSMC has brought more than 3,500 jobs to the state, and an entire economy has sprung up to support the company’s Arizona operation. Much like in Taiwan — where the company accounts for nearly one-tenth of Taiwan’s gross domestic product — TSMC has become, if not the center of the universe, then at least a galaxy unto itself. The company controls an estimated 70 percent of the global chip market, and its contracts with Apple and Nvidia alone make up more than one-third of its annual revenue. (Apple and Nvidia design their own chips, but they don’t produce them. The complex manufacturing process is instead largely outsourced to TSMC.) TSMC has changed swaths of Phoenix — its landscape, its industries — and it has brought with it jobs and prosperity. Locals fear that the new hyperscale data center developments will do the former but not the latter, consuming resources while contributing little to the community. Mackay, who has worked as an economic developer for over 30 years, didn’t experience significant pushback when she helped court data center developments in the past. “The first 10 data centers I did look like pretty little office buildings,” she said. The new developments being proposed are neither pretty nor little. Where earlier data centers were inconspicuous, the hyperscale facilities developers want to build in Arizona — often on rural farm or desert land — are both massive and incongruous. item.title: ESPN’s Pat McAfee speaks out about ‘death threats’ targeting him and his family
item.description: ESPN personality Pat McAfee has spoken out about death threats directed at him and his family, revealing the personal toll of sustained online backlash. The former NFL punter shared a lengthy statement on X, describing his fears and the security concerns surrounding his work on College GameDay . McAfee said he had avoided his mentions and direct messages after receiving threatening messages earlier this month. However, he believes the threats remain widespread. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DM’s this month since these back to back days but.. I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee wrote. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” MORE: Utah, ESPN share statements amid Pat McAfee ‘College GameDay’ tension He also expressed concern about messages targeting his wife, daughter, and son. “It’s a weird time,” McAfee said. “The things that get said about what my daughter and son and wife deserve are all rather wild as well.” McAfee’s statement followed renewed criticism after the University of Utah shared a video mocking him on its official account. He also referenced a New York Times piece that he felt contributed to the negative attention surrounding him. Pat McAfee recalls heightened security at Tennessee Pat McAfee speaks during McAfee’s “Kicking is Easy” Contest at ESPN’s College GameDay at The Grove in Oxford, Miss. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) McAfee also detailed the security concerns surrounding last year’s College GameDay appearance in Tennessee. He said authorities feared a possible copycat incident following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. “The world, in front of the entire internet, just proved that we had gotten to a rather extreme place,” McAfee said. According to McAfee, the FBI, Disney security, Tennessee State Police, Knoxville police, and university police worked together to protect the event. He recalled that a bulletproof vest was even suggested as a precaution. “FBI snipers were sent down there, huge presence of police… it was a surreal moment,” McAfee explains. “The conversation about the death threats I had been receiving in life was definitely a huge topic. I don’t think it was the FBI that suggested the Bullet Proof Vest, but it was certainly an idea presented by one of the security groups. “We had no idea what to expect. Nobody had been in that type of situation before.” Despite the fear, he praised the security teams and students who supported him during the broadcast. He said he had never felt safer or more appreciative of the people around him that morning. McAfee believes the backlash intensified after his comments about Algerian Olympic gold medal-winning boxer Imane Khelif were presented without what he considered important context. He said subsequent mistakes and misquotes repeatedly fueled further hostility. MORE: Pat McAfee recounts terrible Utah College GameDay experience with tasteless Charlie Kirk refer

item.title: SpaceX's Starfall capsule delivers cargo for US Air Force in landmark 'point to point' space mission
item.description: null The U.S. Air Force is opening up about the SpaceX Starfall cargo capsule it flew on a recent rideshare mission to orbit — and showing off what the capsule carried. The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) completed a point-to-point rocket cargo delivery test using the secretive uncrewed reentry vehicle, confirming on social media its recovery of the package in the Pacific Ocean. "With support from SpaceX , the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown," the AFRL wrote in an X post on Oct. 26. The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as a part of SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 20 . Starfall carried a number of AFRL-developed cargo pods designed to transport military equipment through space and back to Earth . The successful recovery of the pods marks a big step forward in the Air Force's effort to examine the viability of point-to-point (P2D) rocket cargo missions. "This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the Future Force," said AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly in a press release on Oct. 20. Photos included in the AFRL social media post show military personnel unpacking a recovered cargo pod for inspection. Each pod contained sensors to monitor temperature conditions through launch, reentry and splashdown, as well as to measure the shock and vibration forces exerted on its cargo. For its first Starfall mission, AFRL packed its cargo pods with representative items like medical equipment, food ration packs and other military kit that might be helpful for surviving an emergency somewhere that's tough to reach via conventional transportation. To that end, AFRL said it also conducted a fit check of a UNI-PAC III life raft inside Starfall, which could potentially be included in future tests. With support from SpaceX, the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. AFRL Each pod contained representative mission equipment to study the effects of temperature, shock, and vibration of the cargo environments during launch and reentry. item.dc:creator: Josh Dinner
item.content:encoded: null The U.S. Air Force is opening up about the SpaceX Starfall cargo capsule it flew on a recent rideshare mission to orbit — and showing off what the capsule carried. The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) completed a point-to-point rocket cargo delivery test using the secretive uncrewed reentry vehicle, confirming on social media its recovery of the package in the Pacific Ocean. "With support from SpaceX , the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown," the AFRL wrote in an X post on Oct. 26. The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as a part of SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 20 . Starfall carried a number of AFRL-developed cargo pods designed to transport military equipment through space and back to Earth . The successful recovery of the pods marks a big step forward in the Air Force's effort to examine the viability of point-to-point (P2D) rocket cargo missions. "This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the Future Force," said AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly in a press release on Oct. 20. Photos included in the AFRL social media post show military personnel unpacking a recovered cargo pod for inspection. Each pod contained sensors to monitor temperature conditions through launch, reentry and splashdown, as well as to measure the shock and vibration forces exerted on its cargo. For its first Starfall mission, AFRL packed its cargo pods with representative items like medical equipment, food ration packs and other military kit that might be helpful for surviving an emergency somewhere that's tough to reach via conventional transportation. To that end, AFRL said it also conducted a fit check of a UNI-PAC III life raft inside Starfall, which could potentially be included in future tests. With support from SpaceX, the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. AFRL Each pod contained representative mission equipment to study the effects of temperature, shock, and vibration of the cargo environments during launch and reentry. AFRL With support from @SpaceX, the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. Each pod contained representative mission equipment to study the effects of temperature, shock, and vibration of the cargo environments during launch and reentry. #Readiness https://t.co/yWoND13ur4 October 26, 2026 "Researchers paid special attention to the electronics equipment and survival gear, including a SATCOM-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, survival gear and emergency medical equipment," AFRL said in its release. SpaceX's disk-shaped Starfall capsule made a quiet debut on a Falcon 9 launch in June, and the company has remained relatively quiet about the vehicle to date. Most of what we do know comes from a Federal Aviation Administration environmental assessment published earlier this year. Starfall measures about 3.1 meters across. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Artist rendering of Starfall entering the atmosphere. SpaceX The hockey-puck-looking vehicle measures approximately 10.2 feet (3.1 meters) across and can return up to 2,200 pounds (1,000 kilograms) of cargo from orbit, according to that report. And it sports a carbon fiber heat shield and compressed gas thrusters for attitude control during reentry, as well as a parachute system for precision landings. AFRL will assess the data recovered from the Oct. 20 mission to contribute to its broader Rocket Cargo initiative, which the Air Force hopes can evolve to the transportation of tens of tons of cargo per launch. That would exceed Starfall's mass capacity, but Starfall isn't the only vehicle the military has considered for its Rocket Cargo program. SpaceX's much larger Starship rocket, which is still under development, was a likely candidate for tests at Johnston Atoll , a remote Pacific bird sanctuary where the Air Force proposed building a pair of landing pads for cargo delivery tests. However, those plans were suspended in July 2025 amid environmental concerns, and the status of the search for an alternative site is unclear.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham reveals FBI is watching 20 stalkers as alleged stalker stays jailed
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham says the FBI is monitoring roughly 20 people on her behalf. This revelation lands while her alleged stalker sits in jail. Cunningham, whose WNBA future is in flux ahead of free agency, told Theo Von on the This Past Weekend podcast about the downside of fame. “We do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do,” she said, then added that she has “20 people that the FBI are watching for me. Me alone.” MORE: Steve Kerr takes jab at WNBA Finals’ unusual Game 6 start time What did Cunningham tell Theo Von? Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) dribbles the ball against Las Vegas Aces. | Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images Cunningham said she wasn’t permitted to name the people under watch, but she identified one. “I know one of them, but yeah. I mean, he’s locked away now,” she said, later adding, “His name’s Kevin.” The former Missouri standout then joked about her miniature donkey of the same name, asking, “Do I need to rename Kevin?” Von joked that the donkey might be working for the stalker. Where does Kevin Singh’s case stand? Prosecutors charged Kevin Singh, 49, with stalking, intimidation and harassment after his June 23 arrest, and an affidavit states he hand-delivered a letter and a cologne-sprayed Guns N’ Roses T-shirt to Gainbridge Fieldhouse in September 2025. A detective wrote that Cunningham “feels like she is always watching her back, doesn’t feel safe and is fearful of Kevin Singh.” Singh remains in the Marion County Jail on a $40,000 bond after a judge rejected his bid for a reduction , and his trial is scheduled for early 2027. Cunningham is the second Fever player targeted in a stalking case, after a Texas man who harassed Fever star Caitlin Clark was sentenced in 2025 to 2 1/2 years in prison. Sophie Cunningham’s Fever free agency Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) warms up before playing the Toronto Tempo | Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Cunningham, 30, is an unrestricted free agent after playing 2026 on a one-year, $665,000 deal. She averaged 7.9 points across 43 games. The Fever finished a franchise-record 28-16 before falling to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round. “I don’t know what the offseason holds,” Cunningham said. “A lot of us are under free agency now, so who knows?” General manager Amber Cox said at exit interviews that “Sophie has had two really productive years for us, in terms of shooting the basketball.” She answered no when asked whether off-court attention would affect that evaluation. The Fever then parted ways with Cox and team president Kelly Krauskopf. Indiana’s new front office will decide whether to bring the veteran guard back. “Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people ,” Cunningham said. MORE: 3 landing spots for Sophie Cunningham, including Atlanta Dream — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals plans to launch his own racing academy outside F1
item.description: Motorsport photo At just 20 years old, Andrea Kimi Antonelli is currently busy making the rest of the Formula 1 grid look like a bunch of sluggish retirees. But apparently, casually dominating the 2026 World Championship in a Mercedes isn't quite enough to keep the Italian phenom occupied. In a recent sit-down with Germany's Auto Motor und Sport , Antonelli revealed that he is already plotting his next massive move outside the F1 paddock: building his own driver academy. Following the recent paddock chatter around Lando Norris launching his own junior team , Antonelli wants a piece of the driver-development pie. And given that he literally grew up inside the garage of his father's GT racing team, AKM Motorsport, he knows exactly how brutal the financial ladder can be for a kid with talent but no cash. "We want to build an academy for young people so they get a chance in motorsport," Antonelli told AMUS. "Motorsport is a great but difficult world. It is not easy to get opportunities there. We want to help young drivers get a chance." The Verstappen GT3 FOMO Interestingly, Antonelli isn't focusing his future academy strictly on getting kids into the Formula 1 feeder series. He explicitly noted that professional GT racing is a highly viable, lucrative path - a mindset heavily fuelled by a certain three-time Dutch world champion. Max Verstappen has essentially turned the GT3 endurance world into his own personal side quest, and the rest of the F1 grid is collectively catching FOMO. Antonelli is no exception. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "GT racing is growing strongly right now," Antonelli confirmed to AMUS. "Max is helping to make it more well-known and show the fascination." With that booming popularity in mind, Antonelli wants his future academy to cast a wider net for young drivers. "That doesn't necessarily have to be in Formula 1," he added. "There are also many opportunities in professional GT racing." Fulfilling the ultimate dad dream Before Antonelli starts writing cheques for a full-blown junior academy, he has a much more personal piece of motorsport business to handle. His father, Marco Antonelli, is a former touring car driver who built the highly successful AKM Motorsport outfit. While Kimi has previously tested his dad's GT3 machinery, the two have never actually shared a cockpit during a live race weekend. According to Kimi, that is about to change very soon. We also have joint projects for the future," Antonelli explained. "A dream of my father's is that we race together one day. item.title: Harry Kane makes ultimate gift promise to England and Bayern Munich teammates after emotional Ballon d'Or victory
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has revealed his plans to treat his Bayern Munich and England colleagues to special gifts following his historic Ballon d'Or triumph in London. The 33-year-old striker enjoyed an incredible 2026, scoring a combined 73 goals for club and country to claim football's most prestigious individual prize. Reaching the pinnacle Kane claimed his maiden Ballon d'Or on Monday night, edging out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to secure the prestigious accolade. The 33-year-old was honoured in his home city of London, where he delivered a gracious acceptance speech before celebrating at an exclusive Soho nightclub. The recognition follows a breathtaking 2026 campaign for the prolific frontman. Kane registered a staggering 61 goals in just 51 appearances across all competitions for Bayern Munich, while adding another 12 strikes to his international tally with the Three Lions. Watches and rewards Following his crowning moment, Kane confirmed he will share his success with the players who helped him reach the summit. Sporting an ultra-rare Rolex Daytona valued at almost £1 million during the ceremony, the striker admitted his teammates are already expecting extravagant rewards. Speaking to German outlet BILD , Kane outlined his intention to purchase presents for both his club and international colleagues. "Some of the lads have asked for watches or something like that, so I’ll have to come up with something nice for them, both at Bayern and with England," he revealed. "I’ll look into it and make sure I get everyone a nice gift." Arise, Sir Harry? Kane becomes England's sixth Ballon d'Or winner, joining an elite group that includes Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan, and Michael Owen. His unparalleled achievements have sparked discussions in Downing Street regarding a potential knighthood , adding to the MBE he received in 2019. When asked by BILD about the prospect of becoming a knight, Kane embraced the idea while remaining grounded . "I certainly wouldn't say no - I really appreciate it," he said. "If it came to that, it would be incredible and something I'd be incredibly proud of. But I don't want to get too carried away with it right now." Questioned on how "Sir Harry Kane" sounds, the Bayern talisman added: "It sounds good, but it would feel kind of strange if everyone called me Sir. So for now, I'll just stick with Harry." A historic Wembley homecoming Kane is set for a monumental evening on November 12 when England host Croatia in the UEFA Nations League. The captain is expected to parade his Ballon d'Or trophy around Wembley Stadium before kick-off to celebrate the milestone with the home supporters. The fixture carries enormous historical significance for the striker beyond his recent award. Currently tied with legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton on 125 caps , Kane will surpass him as the most-capped England player of all time if he takes to the pitch, complementing his existing status as the

item.title: Pirates need to add a veteran starting pitcher
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - JULY 19: Paul Skenes #30 of the Pittsburgh Pirates talks with Braxton Ashcraft #35, Mitch Keller #23 and Jared Jones #17 as he exits the game after the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on July 19, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates finished the season with an 82-80 record. The highlight from this year’s team was the offense but the starting pitching was still solid this season. The question is should the Pirates add a veteran free agent arm for next season? The answer in my mind is yes, Pittsburgh absolutely needs to add experience and depth to that starting rotation. This is still a mostly young rotation with Paul Skenes, Jared Jones, Braxton Ashcraft and Bubba Chandler. Mitch Keller is one of the older starters on the club at 30 years old, so this is a very young group. Ashcraft was arguably the top pitcher for the Bucs with a 14-6 record and a 3.65 ERA. While Skenes finished with a 10-11 record 3.82 ERA. While both Keller and Jones missed serious time with injuries. The first veteran pitcher I think the Pirates should look at is Nick Martinez from the Tampa Bay Rays. Martinez helped lead the Rays to the World Series, where he had a 3.10 ERA over 31 starts while earning his first career All-Star nod in 2026. He doesn’t miss a ton of bats, but he averaged an MLB-low 1.30 walks per nine innings this year. The 36-year-old Martinez has a $20 million mutual option for 2027, but he seems likely to decline it and pursue a multi-year deal in free agency this offseason. Another Pitcher is Michael King from the San Diego Padres. King might be a little pricy, but I think he is worth it. The 31-year-old veteran is widely expected to opt out of the three-year, $75 million contract he signed with the Padres last December and re-enter free agency this winter. King struggled to stay healthy in 2025, but he bounced back to post a 3.21 ERA over 32 starts for San Diego this season. There are other names like Freddy Peralta and Tarik Skubal, but those guys will probably be the most expensive starters on the market. The Bucs do have a good starting rotation, but if they add these names or another veteran arm I think it will improve that unit and the team. I understand some of these pitchers might be a little expensive, but this needs to be the offseason where the front office spends money. There is a lot of young potential with this club, and you don’t want to waste it

item.title: Andoni Iraola reacts to Liverpool’s dramatic win over Chelsea
item.description: Andoni Iraola reacts to Liverpool’s dramatic win over Chelsea Andoni Iraola Hails Liverpool Togetherness After Chelsea Shootout Win Liverpool are into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. That is the point. The rest is detail. At Anfield, a 1-1 draw with Chelsea was settled the hard way, with Liverpool winning the shootout 6-5 after goals from Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo, both from the penalty spot before half-time. It was not polished throughout, but cup football rarely cares for polish. It asks whether you survive. Liverpool did. Andoni Iraola made that clear afterwards. “Yeah, at the end in the cup competitions what matters is that you are in the next round and you are in the draw. Lucky for us finishing the right side of the penalty shootout. I finish pleased because the players have done a very big effort today and at least we get the reward of being in the quarter-finals.” That is the correct reading of the night. Liverpool were stretched, they rotated heavily and they still found a way through against strong opposition. There is no need to romanticise it. The effort was real, the reward matters, and the schedule will not get any kinder. IAMGO Liverpool togetherness proving decisive The more revealing point from Iraola was not about the penalties. It was about the mood around the side. Liverpool have had uneven moments this season, but at home there is now a visible sense of connection between team and crowd. Managers talk about energy and belief because they know how quickly both can disappear. Right now, Liverpool have them. item.content:encoded: Andoni Iraola reacts to Liverpool’s dramatic win over Chelsea Andoni Iraola Hails Liverpool Togetherness After Chelsea Shootout Win Liverpool are into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. That is the point. The rest is detail. At Anfield, a 1-1 draw with Chelsea was settled the hard way, with Liverpool winning the shootout 6-5 after goals from Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo, both from the penalty spot before half-time. It was not polished throughout, but cup football rarely cares for polish. It asks whether you survive. Liverpool did. Andoni Iraola made that clear afterwards. “Yeah, at the end in the cup competitions what matters is that you are in the next round and you are in the draw. Lucky for us finishing the right side of the penalty shootout. I finish pleased because the players have done a very big effort today and at least we get the reward of being in the quarter-finals.” That is the correct reading of the night. Liverpool were stretched, they rotated heavily and they still found a way through against strong opposition. There is no need to romanticise it. The effort was real, the reward matters, and the schedule will not get any kinder. IAMGO Liverpool togetherness proving decisive The more revealing point from Iraola was not about the penalties. It was about the mood around the side. Liverpool have had uneven moments this season, but at home there is now a visible sense of connection between team and crowd. Managers talk about energy and belief because they know how quickly both can disappear. Right now, Liverpool have them. Iraola said: “I feel it and I’m very happy to feel it because I think it’s very important. We need to feel what we are feeling now, the players are feeling. They are feeling the support of the ones in the stands and I think when we are all together, we create better atmospheres. Even starting losing, there was ‘Let’s go, come on.’ A lot of the players have given us very good help and now it’s the third game at home where we finish with good feelings. And we have another big one on Sunday and let’s try to finish this four in a row that we had at home in the best way.” That matters more than any neat tactical talking point. When a side concedes first and the stadium stays with them, it changes the game. Liverpool responded, stayed in it, then held their nerve. Cup ties are often decided by that basic level of emotional control. Carabao Cup draw gives Liverpool a familiar problem The quarter-final now brings Bournemouth to Anfield, which adds an obvious layer to the tie. Iraola knows the club well and, by his own admission, would have preferred anyone else. “Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said, ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth…’ For me, it’s special. They know me very well, they are playing very well lately, in a good moment. But it is what it is. We haven’t been very lucky with the draws, we have played Spurs and Chelsea already and now Bournemouth. That is going to be obviously special for me. But we have to earn the right to be in the semi-finals and I hope we can do it here at home again.” He is right about the draw. It has not been generous. Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea, now Bournemouth, there is nothing soft about that route. If Liverpool reach the last four, they will have done it properly. Squad rotation and Trey Nyoni impact Iraola made seven changes and, again, there was no appetite to dress it up as some grand masterplan. Rotation is necessity, not vanity. Liverpool are playing too often to do anything else. “A little bit of everything. When you do the line-ups and the squads, you are not thinking, ‘In case it goes to penalties, I will leave the ones who shoot the penalties for the end.’ No, you are trying to balance the team. We are changing a lot of the players because we need to change. We did seven changes today but even in the Champions League, which are very important games, we are doing always four or five changes. Obviously when I did the last subs, when I put Alexis [Mac Allister] and Alex [Isak] especially, it starts to be in your head, ‘OK, in case of need, they also are the best ones probably you can put.’” One of the beneficiaries was Trey Nyoni, and Iraola was direct in his assessment. “I think he has done very well. Really well. It’s good for the young players especially to live these experiences in cup competitions, where if you lose you are out. We have been losing and then the draw. Then they haven’t been there in the penalty shootout but they lived the feelings. They played under pressure against a very good team. And Trey has finished physically in a good place, so well done, yes.” No overstatement required. Liverpool are through, the squad is contributing, and the togetherness Iraola wants is starting to look real.

item.title: 🎾 German champion under Klopp: Ex-Bundesliga star elite in another sport!
item.description: 🎾 German champion under Klopp: Ex-Bundesliga star elite in another sport! Moritz Leitner has not been an active professional footballer for four years now. After leaving FC Zurich, the midfielder hung up his boots at just 29. But that does not mean Leitner simply put his feet up afterwards. Quite the opposite: the now 33-year-old devoted himself entirely to padel. The increasingly popular sport seems to be right up his street—and he appears to have quite a knack for it, too. Leitner is now ranked 32nd in Germany's padel rankings. He recently spelled out his ambition to 'Sport Bild': "I want to turn professional in padel, too." His tremendous work ethic should help him get there. "I don't think there's a more padel-mad monkey out there than me—with my attitude and my passion for the sport," Leitner said. "Of course, I come from football and don't have the tennis background that most other players have. But I absolutely love it and give a thousand percent every day." 📸 Martin Rose - 2012 Getty Images Another thing in his favour: Leitner knows exactly how to succeed in sport. As a youngster, he won the Bundesliga and the DFB-Pokal with Borussia Dortmund in 2012. A year later, Jürgen Klopp's young guns also made it all the way to the Champions League final. Let's see whether Leitner can reach similar heights in padel... This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: Live: French anti-terrorism prosecutor to give press conference on racist Paris shooting
item.description: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others last week in the town of Trappes, near Paris, was transferred to the Paris Judicial Court on Thursday, where he may be formally charged. France's national anti-terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen is due to speak Thursday at 11am, with his statement to be broadcast live on FRANCE 24.

item.title: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace
item.description: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace Michael Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best players since Bayern Munich signed him from Crystal Palace for a reported €53 million in 2024. In an interview with FC Bayern’s club magazine, "51", board member for sport Max Eberl has revealed what convinced the German champions to sign the French winger. “He had a somewhat unsettled career path: he attended several elite football academies in England. But that kind of background doesn’t necessarily have to be a red flag – facing adversity can also help shape a player," Eberl said. “To get to know a footballer, above all, you have to talk to people who have experienced him as either a teammate or an opponent.” Conversations between Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund and his fellow Austrian Oliver Glasner, who was managing Crystal Palace at the time, proved particularly valuable in assessing Olise. “In Michael’s case, we had the advantage that Oliver Glasner was his manager at Crystal Palace at the time – and our sporting director, Christoph Freund, knows Glasner very well,” Eberl said. "When a manager says, ‘Of course, take him, take him,’ it makes you suspicious. But Glasner said, ‘He still has things to learn – and we could really use him.’ That told you he valued Michael highly. "And then there were the conversations with Michael himself: it’s a pleasure to talk football with him.”

That allowed them to take a week off in the Division II, Region 5 playoffs, which is a big thing in that bracket. This week: Bye. item.title: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona
item.description: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona Real Madrid signed Bernardo Silva as a free agent back in the summer after his contract with Manchester City expired. Los Blancos secured his signature, beating the likes of Barcelona and Atletico Madrid to it, and expectations were high about what he could add to the midfield. However, it has taken some time for him to settle in, and Madrid’s victory over Barca at the Camp Nou seems like a turning point for the Portuguese midfielder. Bernardo Silva delivered his most convincing performance since arriving in the summer, justifying Jose Mourinho’s determination to bring him to the Bernabeu . According to Diario AS , Silva had long dreamed of representing Madrid, but his initial approach was rejected earlier this year. Mourinho’s return changed everything, with the manager personally pushing for his arrival despite interest from several other European clubs. Mourinho’s intervention changed Bernardo Silva’s future After deciding to leave Manchester City, Silva initially struggled to convince Madrid to pursue his signature. Bernardo Silva is slowly coming into his own at Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) His agent, Jorge Mendes, subsequently explored alternative destinations, with Barcelona emerging as a serious possibility. However, during a June meeting with Jose Angel Sanchez and Juni Calafat, Mourinho made his intentions clear. “We need a player like Bernardo Silva. We have to secure his signing,” the Portuguese manager insisted. Once Silva learned of Madrid’s interest, he paused other negotiations and prioritised the move. He eventually joined on a free transfer, signing a contract until 2028. Mourinho’s patience rewarded with impressive Clasico display Despite pushing for his signing, Mourinho deliberately managed Silva’s introduction into the team. He wanted the 32-year-old midfielder to regain his physical sharpness before assuming greater responsibilities. That patience paid off against Barcelona, where Silva helped Madrid dictate the tempo and maintain composure against a much more technical midfield. Will Bernardo be a started in the upcoming games? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His contribution was particularly important because Madrid had originally identified Rodri as their preferred option to provide control in midfield. While Silva is a different player from his former team-mate, he helped Madrid outplay a midfield featuring Rodri. The Clasico also showed why Silva’s experience matters for Madrid. There is no doubt that he will have an important role to play in the coming weeks . Silva has now taken an important step towards establishing himself as a regular starter, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the upcoming games.

item.title: 'She cold': Tyrese Maxey reacts to meeting Caitlin Clark for the first time ever
item.description: Credit: David Berding/Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images Tyrese Maxey starred for the Philadelphia 76ers in their win over the Indiana Pacers, but he experienced another major highlight off the court. The All-Star guard had the opportunity to meet WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark for the first time at the Gainbridge Fieldhouse, which is her home arena with the Indiana Fever. After the game, Maxey spoke about meeting Clark. Tyrese Maxey says he tried ‘not to fan out’ while meeting Caitlin Clark Clark is one of the biggest names in the WNBA. The 24-year-old has taken the women’s game to unprecedented heights, and she has earned a massive fan following as a result. Among her fans appears to be Maxey, who is a superstar himself, but he couldn’t hide his excitement when he met Clark during the 76ers’ win over the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night. Speaking after the game, he said on Wish TV News: “I think that’s the first time I’m really meeting her. Honestly, that’s just like, shoot, another person I like to watch. She cold. She nice. “So seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, you know? It was really cool seeing her. This is her building, she plays here. It was good seeing her. She’s nice.” Maxey’s candid admission that he had to stop himself from fanning out shows the enormous impact Clark has had in the world of basketball. The admiration there is absolutely fantastic to see, and we’re sure Maxey’s reaction to meeting the Indiana Fever star will not be forgotten by fans across the country. Up next for the Sixers is an NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks on Friday night. Maxey will be hoping to continue his good form in that game.

item.title: Law Firm Linked to Elon Musk Started an ‘Election Integrity’ Organization
item.description: The firm that helped set up Elon Musk’s America PAC is behind the new group, which will work with election officials to pursue policies aligned with Donald Trump’s false election fraud claims.

item.title: Will Burnley's Celestini gamble pay off?
item.description: [BBC] Four days after sacking Nicky Hayen, Burnley have wasted little time in bringing in Fabio Celestini to replace him as their new head coach. The 50-year-old from Switzerland won the domestic double in his home country with FC Basel in the 2024-25 season and has never managed in English football. So, are Clarets fans excited to see what Celestini can bring to the table, or has his appointment raised more questions than answers? Let us know your thoughts here and come back later to see a selection of your responses. Latest Burnley news, analysis and fan views Ask about Burnley - what do you want to know?

item.title: FDU basketball to wear jersey patch for special cause this season
item.description: Like a lot of men’s college basketball teams, FDU will debut a patch on its jerseys when the 2026-27 season gets underway next week. Unlike just about everyone else, that patch is not a corporate sponsorship designed to make money. Head coach Jack Castleberry had something else in mind. “What if we found a cause and championed that cause?” he said in pitching his idea to athletics director Jason Young. “It would be an opportunity for us to do some good here.” When the Knights’ take the court at third-ranked Illinois Monday, and for the remainder of their schedule, the upper right corner of their jerseys will read “NDSS” and in smaller letters, “National Down Syndrome Society.” The Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit's mission, “to create a world where individuals with Down syndrome thrive,” is close to Castleberry’s heart. His youngest daughter, 2-year-old Avery, has Down syndrome. And for Castleberry, his wife Kara and their two older daughters (ages 7 and 5), it’s been an eye-opening experience. “I think there’s a lot of misunderstanding out there about what Down syndrome actually is and what the lives are like for those who have Down syndrome,” said Castleberry, who lives in River Edge in Bergen County. “It’s not this terrible thing that I believe most people think it is.” When he and Kara found out Avery would be born with Down syndrome, “it shakes you a little bit” he said. But as he explained, borrowing a line from a book he read on the subject, that was the last bad day. “I can’t speak to everybody’s experience, but my kid is the happiest kid of the three I have,” he said. “She is such a joy. I never thought I would say something like this, but when you’re in front of her, no matter who you are, she sees you. She looks into your soul and there’s a genuine connection. That, I certainly didn’t expect. “You walk into the room with her and your day just brightens up.” Part of Castleberry’s motivation was that he noticed “stuff out there (on social media) about Down syndrome that wasn’t accurate, and to me that was sad,” he said, adding that some of it reached the point where “I felt a little bit threatened for my daughter.” Then he realized he’s got a pretty big forum – FDU’s opener at Illinois will be nationally televised by the Big Ten Network – and the ability to do something about that. “I genuinely proud, and I’m thankful that our administration is not only willing to consider something like this, but adamant about us doing it,” Castleberry said. For the National Down Syndrome Society, this partnership is the first of its kind. “It was really nice to be able to connect with Jack, and that means so much to us because families are at the core of what we do,” said Michelle Sagan, the nonprofit’s director of communications and marketing, who has a sister with Down syndrome. “We hope people see the patch, hear about Down syndrome on the broadcasts, and it really helps people understand our population.” The partnership will extend beyond a patch.

For the National Down Syndrome Society, this partnership is the first of its kind. “It was really nice to be able to connect with Jack, and that means so much to us because families are at the core of what we do,” said Michelle Sagan, the nonprofit’s director of communications and marketing, who has a sister with Down syndrome. “We hope people see the patch, hear about Down syndrome on the broadcasts, and it really helps people understand our population.” The partnership will extend beyond a patch. Sagan said the National Down Syndrome Society will be bringing a contingent to FDU’s Jan. 30 home game against Stonehill, which also has a member of the coaching staff with a Down syndrome connection. “This is monumental, because visibility matters so much,” Sagan said. “If people don’t have a personal connection to Down syndrome like Jack does, this is a starting point for learning more.” Before moving forward with the patch, Castleberry wanted to make sure his players were on board. “They know my daughter has Down syndrome, and I had a long conversation with them about it,” he said. “I said, ‘I don’t want you guys to be uncomfortable, but this is how we can help.’” Then he wanted to hear what they thought. “We have a player on our team who has a relative with a developmental disability,” Castleberry said. “When I finished talking he spoke up and said, ‘Hey coach, make my patch the biggest.’” To learn more about the National Down Syndrome Society, visit www.ndss.org . Jerry Carino has covered the New Jersey sports scene since 1996 and the college basketball beat since 2003. Contact him at jcarino@gannettnj.com . item.title: Golden Nuggets: Go… Panthers?
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 19: San Francisco 49ers' DeForest Buckner (99), right, sacks Green Bay Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (12), left, during the first quarter of the NFC Championship game at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Jan. 19, 2020. (Randy Vazquez/MediaNews Group/The Mercury News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images It’s an NFC match-up tonight, so I guess mathemetically you’d want the Packers to lose so they don’t gain any ground on the 49ers. The Panthers would improve to 4-3 and lead their division, while the Packers are last in the NFC North. I’m not looking forward to technically having to root for Dallas, but at least I get to root for Jim Harbaugh’s Chargers and the Chicago Bears. After bringing back DeForest Buckner, will the 49ers make more trades? “An addition such as Mack — or other potentially available edge rushers like the Jets’ Will McDonald IV, Cardinals’ Josh Sweat or Bucs’ Yaya Diaby — would make sense to round out San Francisco’s rotation for a reasonable cost in terms of what they need to give up. As with Bosa, the team has to be cautious with Evans to ensure he’s ready for the playoff push. Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., Cleveland’s Jerry Jeudy and the Colts’ Josh Downs (who requested a trade Wednesday) are among the wideouts who could be available for something less than a premium draft pick. If the Niners truly want to swing for the fences, they could try to pry loose a superstar. Raiders end Maxx Crosby and Jets wideout Garrett Wilson are names that move the needle, but they’re unlikely trade candidates barring a significant offer — one with multiple top picks, probably including multiple first-rounders.” 49ers release struggling cornerba ck “Atlanta picked on Jones in coverage. He allowed four of his five targets to be completed for 49 yards, allowing a passer rating of 107.5. In five games this season, Jones was targeted over 30% of the time when he was on the field. Teams were not scared of him. Against Atlanta, Jones allowed 5.8 yards of separation on five targets. Add in the penalties, and he became unplayable, since the run defense and tackling were a struggle. The 49ers will actually save money by releasing Jones, according to Over the Cap. He signed a one-year deal, and the contract has no guaranteed money beyond what appears to be a $140,000 signing bonus. Cornerback Nate Hobbs remains on the injured reserve. That’s a potential veteran replacement in the second half if the 49ers don’t address cornerback ahead of the trade deadline.” Defensive lineman? Check. Next on the 49ers’ shopping list: wide receiver “Thomas isn’t the only disappointing first-round pick who might be moved: The Chargers (0-6) could part with Quentin Johnston (6-2, 208), the 21st pick in 2023 who has eight catches in five games after he had a career-best 735 yards receiving last season.”

item.title: Giants team up with USA Rugby to tutor NJ high school players
item.description: JERSEY CITY — Even as he cringed at what New York Giants ' management might think, Sisi Mauigoa couldn't help but toss the rugby ball around at Lincoln Park in Jersey City on Oct. 28. After all, the rookie guard played rugby and volleyball growing up in American Samoa before realizing "there was a better future in football." He and NFL teammate Jarrod Gray, a former pro rugby player from Sydney, Australia, showed off their moves for Hudson Catholic players at a clinic on Oct. 28. Three members of the United States women's national rugby team – prop Reece Woods, lock Malia Isaacs and center Kennedy Feasby – also stepped in for tackling drills. Only minimal touching allowed to preserve everyone's health. The women also took their turn throwing and catching the football. Mauioga, a massive 6-foot-6, 335-pound lineman, even awkwardly demonstrated his scoring celebration, which he hopes to do in the end zone someday. "It warmed my heart," Isaacs said of the young players. "I believe in them so much. ... The kids had a spark in them. If they want to go on, they'll be great." Check out our exclusive photo gallery from the USA Rugby and New York Giants clinic, then scroll down for the rest of the story. International doubleheader in NJ The national rugby teams will play an international doubleheader on Oct. 30 at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The women's Eagles are slated to face England in the final match of the WXV Global Series, followed by the men's Eagles' rematch against Australia XV. The American women have won the first four matches in the series , toppling Ireland, Wales and Italy twice. Australia shook off back-to-back losses to New Zealand's All Blacks earlier this month by defeating the U.S. men, 61-12, on Oct. 24 in Nashville. From rugby to American football A rugby ball is wider and heavier than an American football, with more rounded ends and no laces. A pass looks more like a two-handed heave than a traditional quarterback spiral. Points are scored similarly: by carrying the ball beyond the goal line or kicking between the posts. Tackling isn't very different in a scrum or at the line of scrimmage either. "The physicality is the big thing that transfers over," said Gray, a 6-foot-7, 318-pound lineman who is part of the NFL's International Player Pathway , which gives elite athletes from overseas an opportunity to develop football skills. "The footwork, though, is much more detailed in the NFL. Having good feet helped me transition over. Rugby league is a lot more fitness, a lot more endurance. 'Tackle, get up, make the next one.' American football is more based on power, strength, explosiveness. That's what I have to adapt to." Some of Hudson Catholic's rugby players do double duty with the football team, and went straight from the clinic to practice for the Oct. 29 consolation game against Passaic. Only minimal touching allowed to preserve everyone's health. The women also took their turn throwing and catching the football. Mauioga, a massive 6-foot-6, 335-pound lineman, even awkwardly demonstrated his scoring celebration, which he hopes to do in the end zone someday. American football is more based on power, strength, explosiveness. That's what I have to adapt to." Some of Hudson Catholic's rugby players do double duty with the football team, and went straight from the clinic to practice for the Oct. 29 consolation game against Passaic. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Casillas, a former Giants linebacker from New Brunswick, kept a close eye on the Hawks. He gave tips on quick cuts to both the boys and girls, and not even the NFL players were exempt from teasing. Hudson Catholic junior Mackenzie Harriett-Clay and her twin brother Kellen have been playing tackle rugby since fourth grade, but started flag years earlier. She'd never dreamed to have USA Eagles or NFL players at practice. "I can learn when to tackle, keeping a straight line, staying low, being able to shift," said Harriett-Clay, who lives in Carteret. "It feels great. I'm very grateful for it. Not a lot of people will have this chance. I have to work hard and prove I'm a good player." This article originally appeared on Morristown Daily Record: Giants team up with USA Rugby to tutor NJ high school players

item.title: Travis Kelce explains exactly why Seattle Seahawks are so hard to play against right now
item.description: Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Travis Kelce breaks down what Mike MacDonald has done with the Seattle Seahawks which makes them so difficult to beat. The Kansas City Chiefs were handed their first loss of the season in pretty spectacular fashion by the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The reigning Super Bowl champions won 20-3, completely shutting off Kenneth Walker III and Patrick Mahomes. It was no mean feat, as both have been in fine form to start the year. Travis Kelce has been looking like his old self for the most part, too. He wasn’t able to do much either, though. Kelce had four receptions in the game for 44 yards. He spoke about what makes the Seattle defence special. Travis Kelce breaks down Mike MacDonald’s defensive preference which makes Seattle tough The Seattle Seahawks have been the NFL’s best defence by total yards allowed this season, giving up just 233.9 yards per game. That’s No. 1 in the league. They’ve been excellent at limiting their opponents, with a sizeable gap between them and the second-ranked Minnesota Vikings. Kelce, in conversation with his brother Jason on their podcast, addressed how head coach Mike MacDonald is able to make that happen. “I feel like every time I face McDonald, he stays true to his style, and he has the personnel to be able to execute how he wants to,” the tight end said. “He’s going to kind of want to keep everything in front of him in terms of the back end of things. “But he’s always got an unbelievable D-line that just makes it tough to get to the second level on your double teams. It really forces you to be great on the backside of runs where, it’s typically the ball ends up coming back to that gap.” MacDonald became the first head coach in NFL history to win the Super Bowl while still being the primary defensive play-caller. The Seahawks are just 4-3 this season, but with their defense, one can never really write them off. item.title: College football games on TV today: Full schedule, times, channels, live streams to watch NCAA Week 9
item.description: College football games on TV today: Full schedule, times, channels, live streams to watch NCAA Week 9 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After another weekend of upsets reshuffled the Top 25, several more key matchups await this weekend ahead of the first College Football Playoff rankings release next week. The marquee attraction is one of the sport's great rivalries, with No. 3 Georgia and No. 17 Florida facing off in Atlanta instead of their traditional neutral site in Jacksonville, Florida. Each is coming off a bye heading into a game that could further scramble an already complicated SEC postseason picture. The only other matchup of ranked teams this weekend features No. 13 Texas Tech looking to bounce back from its stunning loss to Cincinnati with a home game against No. 22 Arizona, which has been cruising since an early loss at BYU. There are other intriguing games on tap, though, including Cincinnati going for another upset at home against No. 6 Utah, No. 1 Miami heading on the road to face Bill Belichick and North Carolina, and No. 2 Ohio State going cross-country for a matchup with USC. All that and much more awaits in Week 9 of the college football season. Here's when and where to watch every game. item.title: Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez reflects on La Masia journey and life away from football
item.description: Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez reflects on La Masia journey and life away from football Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez has reflected on the people and experiences that shaped his football journey, revealing how his first coach recognised his potential and why his parents have remained central to his success. In an interview with GQ (h/t SPORT ), the Spaniard also discussed his childhood in El Campillo, his move to La Masia and the simple routines that help him unwind away from football. His reflections come during a period in which Fermin is enjoying success both personally and professionally, following a difficult summer disrupted by an injury that ruled him out of representing Spain at the 2026 World Cup. Fermin recalls early signs of his footballing potential Fermin’s journey began in El Campillo, where his first coach , Rafael, quickly recognised that the youngster possessed qualities that could take him far in the game. “My first coach at El Campillo, from the moment he saw me, always told my parents that he saw something different in me. “His name is Rafael and I think he was the first person to coach me who saw something special in me, as well as the potential to go far in football,” he said. Football was already central to Fermin’s childhood, with much of his free time spent playing with friends. Fermin Lopez has looked back at his early career. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His memories of those early years reflect a passion that extended well beyond organised training. “We used to play on the pitches; we’d sneak off to play, and I always had footballs in my room. The ball has always been my best friend, and football has been with me ever since.” Barcelona midfielder credits parents for his development Moving to La Masia at the age of 13 marked a major change in Fermin’s life, taking him away from the familiar surroundings of home. Throughout that transition and the challenges that followed, he identified his parents as his most dependable source of support. “Ever since I went to La Masia at the age of 13, I’d say my parents have been a cornerstone in my life and throughout my entire journey. “Whenever I’ve been feeling down, I’ve turned to them and they’ve supported and helped me. I’d say they’re two cornerstone figures who’ve always been there for me and have stood by me throughout this process.” Their encouragement has remained important throughout his development into a Barcelona first-team midfielder. FIFA, Fortnite and time with his partner Fermin likes to switch off from football every once in a while. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Away from training and competition, Fermin prefers relatively straightforward ways to spend his limited free time. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His memories of those early years reflect a passion that extended well beyond organised training. “We used to play on the pitches; we’d sneak off to play, and I always had footballs in my room. The ball has always been my best friend, and football has been with me ever since.” Barcelona midfielder credits parents for his development Moving to La Masia at the age of 13 marked a major change in Fermin’s life, taking him away from the familiar surroundings of home. I’d say they’re two cornerstone figures who’ve always been there for me and have stood by me throughout this process.” Their encouragement has remained important throughout his development into a Barcelona first-team midfielder. FIFA, Fortnite and time with his partner Fermin likes to switch off from football every once in a while. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Away from training and competition, Fermin prefers relatively straightforward ways to spend his limited free time. Walking his dog and going out with his partner provide opportunities to relax and take a break from the demands of professional football. “I really enjoy going for walks with my dog. I’ve said it many times, but I really do enjoy it. “I like going out just with my partner, chatting, switching off. I play video games, watch TV series – the usual sort of things.” Gaming is another favourite pastime, although the midfielder admitted that his competitive personality follows him away from the pitch. “The two games I play most are FIFA and Fortnite. At the moment I’m playing a lot of FIFA with my Barça teammates… I’m very competitive and I get quite annoyed, ” he concluded.

item.title: Marc Marquez wary of MotoGP title rival Jorge Martin at Sepang: "Adrenaline is the best painkiller"
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP points leader Marc Marquez claims to be wary of Jorge Martin's potential if his rival is passed fit to race at Sepang this weekend. Martin fractured his wrist in a heavy crash during the sprint race in Australia last weekend, falling 10 points behind Marquez in the championship. Factory Aprilia rider Martin has been declared fit to take part in Friday's opening session in Malaysia, but most expect him to be compromised if he races at all. Read Also: Jorge Martin braced for “really difficult, painful” MotoGP weekend with broken arm His Ducati counterpart Marquez said he wasn't buying that line. He referenced the stricter medical clearance threshold introduced since Marquez seriously compounded injuries by returning too soon after a crash at Jerez in 2020. "I feel and I believe that with the new protocols we have after my injury at Jerez, if they declare him fit, it means that he's able to ride," said the 33-year-old. "And if he's able to ride, he will be at a very high level because adrenaline is the best painkiller." Speaking in his native Spanish, Marquez went a step further in talking up his opponent: "I’m not just confident he’ll be fast on track, I'm certain of it. It won’t change how I approach my own work, but I’ll certainly be pushing to the maximum." Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team The Spaniard also welcomed his countryman's efforts to race in Malaysia, saying it was better for the show. "Yeah, of course for the championship fight it's better that Jorge is there. I'm happy to see Martin on track." While Marquez offers soundbites designed not to tempt fate, it is worth pointing out that he landed what appeared to be a major psychological blow on Martin at Phillip Island. The 2024 world champion fell off during a close battle with Marquez , despite being the faster rider. That mental setback came on top of a not dissimilar mistake at the previous sprint in Indonesia, in which he was also quicker than Marquez. On that occasion, Martin was forced to give Marquez the lead due to tyre pressure concerns, but erred as he attempted to hit the front again. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

(Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Getty Shai Gilgeous-Alexander did not see action in the fourth quarter of the Oklahoma City Thunder’s 120-96 loss to the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night. The loss was the first defeat of the Thunder this season. In the game, they missed Alex Caruso, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Nikola Topic, and Thomas Sorber. Gilgeous-Alexander played just 28 minutes in the game. Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 21 points, 6 rebounds, and 2 assists as the team got blown out. Gilgeous-Alexander sat out the entirety of the fourth quarter as the team got buried by double digits entering the final frame. With what happened in the past few days for the Thunder, SGA’s benching caused some concern about his health. Fortunately, there is nothing to be worried about, as Gilgeous-Alexander is healthy and he just sat out the fourth quarter to allow the bench players to get their reps against a solid team like the Mavericks. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Draws Lessons From Thunder’s 1st Loss In The Season Getty OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – OCTOBER 22: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder celebrates with fans during the second half against the Denver Nuggets at Paycom Center on October 22, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has some key takeaways about the Thunder’s first loss. Overall, he wants to be better moving forward. “I think there were multiple things. You have to be better on the glass. I’m obviously smaller out there now, so it’s a little more challenging, but we have to be tougher. That helps us get out there and play faster, too,” he said. “Especially with guys down, I have to be better if we’re going to have a chance to win games. If we clean those two things up, the game looks a little different. But yeah, they were the ones who won.” It was also the Thunder’s third game in four days and many things have happened since the first game last Sunday. Here’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander after OKC’s loss to Dallas pic.twitter.com/Vo1mupqbBH — Justin Martinez (@Justintohoops) October 29, 2026 Thunder Still Deal With Emotions From Horrific Injuries Getty OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – OCTOBER 26: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder handles the ball during the second half against the Phoenix Suns at Paycom Center on October 26, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) SGA talked about the emotions the team has been dealing with since the season-ending injuries of Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. It hasn’t been anything we haven’t experienced before. It’s part of it. It is what it is. “I don’t feel any more drained, tired or stressed than I have at any other point in my career. It’s been a long season, but yeah, it’s been a season,” he said before talking about Williams and Wallace still talking to the team. “I mean, we’re teammates, we’re brothers, we’re friends. We knew that was never going to leave us. It’ll be like that for the rest of our lives. Having those guys around is always good.” Jalen Williams sustained a dislocated left ankle and a fractured left fibula, an injury requiring surgery that is expected to sideline him for several months and potentially the rest of the season. Meanwhile, Cason Wallace suffered a torn labrum in his left shoulder, also necessitating surgery with a projected recovery timeline of roughly five to six months. The Thunder are leaning on guard Ajay Mitchell and rookie Jared McCain to step up and shoulder the primary scoring load alongside superstar Gilgeous-Alexander. The rotational strain has been worsened by short-term injuries to Caruso and Holmgren. Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault has inserted center Isaiah Hartenstein and forward Kenrich Williams into an overhauled starting lineup, while also relying on deep bench options and rookies like Bennett Stirtz, Josh Dix, and Aday Mara to maximize their roster. item.title: Gov Eno Proposes ₦200,000 Bursary For A’Ibom Students, ₦250,000 For Others
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has announced plans to increase the annual bursary for students in public tertiary institutions from ₦50,000 to ₦200,000, while students studying Medicine, Law and Engineering would receive ₦250,000. Eno announced the development in a fireside chat on the second day of the Ibom Ignite 2026 Conference at Ibom Hall, Uyo, on Wednesday. He explained that the proposed increase would take effect if he wins the February 2027 governorship election and is sworn in for a second term. Governor Eno said the increase was intended to help students manage their tuition fees more easily, adding that his administration would sustain free and compulsory education at the primary and secondary school levels. He also urged beneficiaries of the ₦50 million Ibom Ignite business grant to use the funds judiciously to grow their businesses and improve their livelihoods. The state governor described the grant as seed capital for business development, warning that beneficiaries should not spend it on personal pleasure or unproductive ventures. “A seed not properly planted and tended was as good as dead,” he said, encouraging the young entrepreneurs to invest the funds carefully and work towards achieving their business goals. Speaking on his administration’s support for vulnerable residents, Eno said more than 500 Compassionate Homes had been built for less privileged people across the state’s 31 local government areas. He added that each beneficiary received a ₦500,000 business grant to support their livelihood. Governor Eno pledged to build an additional 1,000 Compassionate Homes and provide the accompanying business grants across the state’s wards if re-elected for a second term. He also highlighted youth development programmes at the Dakkada Skills Acquisition Centre, the Ibom Leadership and Entrepreneurial Development Centre (Ibom-LED), and the newly completed youth development centres across the state. Earlier, the conference guest speaker and Chief Executive Officer of Strategy House Limited, Dr. Maxwell Ubah, urged young people to develop a mindset that supports economic growth and social relevance. Speaking on the theme, “Change Your Thinking, Change Your Future,” Ubah said wealth creation begins with the mind. Citing Singapore and Dubai, he noted that sound economic policies and transformative leadership could help overcome geographical limitations. He encouraged young people to see problems as opportunities for enterprise and identified potential, problems, passion, and possibilities as key ingredients for success. Other speakers at the conference included the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Hensek Integrated Services Limited, Engr. Uwem Stephen Okoko; Akwa Ibom State Commissioner for Sports, Paul Bassey; the Governor’s Delivery Adviser on Tourism, Sir Charles Udoh; the Sole Administrator of Ibom Paint and Programme Director at Ibom-LED, Ime Uwah; and the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Start Innov
