item.title: How Kimi Antonelli can win 2026 F1 title in Mexico City without even finishing race
item.description: Kimi Antonelli is on the cusp of becoming Formula 1 ’s youngest-ever world champion and looks set to claim the 2026 drivers’ title at the Mexican Grand Prix . The 20-year-old has made a mockery of the pre-season predictions which put his Mercedes teammate George Russell as the title favourite, with nine grand prix victories and 15 podiums in total. After his win in Austin, Antonelli currently has a 123-point lead over Russell with five rounds (and no sprint races) remaining this season, assuming F1 fulfils its end-of-season schedule with Qatar and Abu Dhabi. If those races can’t take place due to the conflict in the Middle East, a one-off round would conclude the campaign in Imola. Antonelli is also aiming to become the sport’s youngest world champion in its 76-year history. The current holder of this accolade is Sebastian Vettel, who won his first championship in 2010 at 23 years and 134 days. The Italian would also become only the third-ever driver – after Lewis Hamilton and Jacques Villeneuve – to win the championship in just his second season. Here’s how Antonelli can win the title this weekend in Mexico City - without even racing: Ninth or higher will guarantee the title Antonelli has a 123-point lead over second-placed Russell and a 124-point lead over Hamilton, with 125 points left on the table this season. After this round in Mexico City, there will be 100 points left to play for. As such, to win the title in Mexico City, Antonelli only needs to finish ninth or higher in Sunday’s race . Ninth would give him two points and while Russell could win the race and be 100 points behind, the Briton cannot catch the Italian’s race wins tally for the season, which is the tiebreaker if scores are level. However, even if Antonelli retires or finishes outside the top-10, he could still pick up the title. At a minimum, Russell or Hamilton need to win the grand prix to stretch the title race to Brazil next week. Antonelli has a 123-point lead (AP) Top-10 - Driver standings ahead of Mexico City Grand Prix 1. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) - 365 points 2. George Russell (Mercedes) - 242 points 3. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) - 241 points 4. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) - 236 points 5. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) - 233 points 6. Lando Norris (McLaren) - 211 points 7. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) - 144 points 8. Isack Hadjar (Racing Bulls) - 105 points 9. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) - 77 points 10. Pierre Gasly (Alpine) - 42 points

After this round in Mexico City, there will be 100 points left to play for. As such, to win the title in Mexico City, Antonelli only needs to finish ninth or higher in Sunday’s race . Ninth would give him two points and while Russell could win the race and be 100 points behind, the Briton cannot catch the Italian’s race wins tally for the season, which is the tiebreaker if scores are level. However, even if Antonelli retires or finishes outside the top-10, he could still pick up the title. At a minimum, Russell or Hamilton need to win the grand prix to stretch the title race to Brazil next week. item.title: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United
item.description: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United After 11 Premiership games, and having played every other team once, Celtic find themselves four points clear at the top of the table. Martin O’Neill’s side are four points better off than at this stage last season and have won nine out of their 11 games in the campaign. Indeed, the only points dropped have been in two home games, and while Thursday night’s 2-2 draw with Dundee United saw the Champions maintain their Premiership lead, there was also a sense of frustration that it couldn’t have been extended. However, reflecting on the game, Martin O’Neill said that in a game his side should have won, over the course of the campaign it could still prove to be a valuable point gained, given the team had to come from behind. “It was a tough old game for us,” the Celtic manager told CelticPlayer . “I thought the second half performance was very strong and we had attack after attack. Yet, remarkably, they could have scored on a breakaway. “It was a big, big second half for us and we deserved the equaliser at least. And I just thought we were going to come up trumps towards the end. “The boys have given a lot in the game and they'll have to do the same again in a few days’ time. “We're going to be playing against Falkirk who are up for the game themselves. So it's just resting up, doing a little bit of work, but not that much because the games have been coming thick and fast.” CELTICPLAYER UNIQUE ANGLE Celtic drew 2-2 with Dundee United on Wednesday night to remain four points clear at the top of the table. Camilo Duran opened the scoring in th egame while Liam Scales provided a second-half equaliser for the Hoops. Fixtures Celtic Vs. Dundee United - Wed, Oct 28th 2026, 19:45 Final score: 2 - 2

item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following big road win over Pacers
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS -- The Philadelphia 76ers rode the roller coaster on Thursday in their road matchup with the Indiana Pacers . The Sixers led by 10 at halftime, but then got blitzed in the third quarter when the Pacers outscored them 36-13, but Philadelphia responded by outscoring Indiana 39-21 in the fourth to win it 114-109 on the road. Tyrese Maxey exploded in the fourth and then led Philadelphia with 27 points and five rebounds, Jaylen Brown added 20 points and 10 rebounds, Joel Embiid had 21 points and 11 rebounds, while LeBron James added 13 points, five rebounds, and 10 assists. Anfernee Simons had 20 points, and VJ Edgecombe added eight points and seven rebounds. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers after a win over the Pacers: Maxey's big fourth quarter The Sixers needed somebody out on the perimeter to do something on the offensive end in order to close this game out. Through three quarters, Maxey only had 10 points on 4-for-10 shooting. Then, the 2-time All-Star flipped the switch as he scored 17 points on 4-for-8 shooting and shot 7-for-8 from the foul line. He flipped the game on its head and he was the big reason why the Sixers were able to walk away with the win. The Pacers deserve credit for being physical with him and not allowing anything easy, but Maxey breaking out was a huge storyline in this win. "JB was on me beginning of the fourth quarter just about being aggressive and doing what I do," Maxey said after the win. "I think I just kind of let the game come to me. We've got a lot of different guys out here that can do a lot of different things. So it's going to be nights where shots are limited. That's just how the game flows and that's OK." The team turning a corner in the fourth Along with Maxey, the Sixers as a team just played much better. The Pacers built such a big lead and had a raucous Gainbridge Fieldhouse behind them. Nobody would have blamed the Sixers if they just gave up, but they didn't. This team dug deep, which is a great characteristic to have, and they completely turned the game around in order to get the job done and earn a big win in the season series between these two teams. James had four points and four assists in the fourth, Embiid had seven points, Maxey took over, and the Sixers locked in defensively as they head the Pacers to 6-for-20 shooting in the final frame and Indiana was 0-for-7 from deep. "Just played harder," said Embiid. "Obviously, it's easier when you make shots, but it started on defense. Better defensive intensity, then offensively, hit a few shots, able to get in transition." Simons breaks through The Sixers have had their ups and downs when it comes to 3-point shooting to begin the season. They haven't put up as many 3s and they haven't converted on enough 3s to make the offense flow in a more cohesive way. item.title: RBL through to the DFB-Pokal round of 16: All you need to know about the draw
item.description: RBL through to the DFB-Pokal round of 16: All you need to know about the draw The draw for the DFB-Pokal round of 16 will take place at the German Football Museum in Dortmund on Sunday, 1st November, from 19:15 CET . Here’s everything you need to know. When will the next round take place? The round of 16 ties will be played on 1st and 2nd December , with the remaining rounds taking place in the new year. The quarter-finals are scheduled for 2nd/3rd and 9th/10th February 2027, followed by the semi-finals on 20th/21st April. The competition will conclude with the final at Berlin’s Olympiastadion on Saturday, 29th May 2027 , one week after the final Bundesliga matchday. Which teams have reached the round of 16? Bundesliga FC Bayern Borussia Dortmund RB Leipzig VfB Stuttgart Bayer Leverkusen SC Freiburg Eintracht Frankfurt 1. FC Köln FC Augsburg Borussia Mönchengladbach 2. Bundesliga Hertha BSC 1. FC Kaiserslautern VfL Bochum SV Darmstadt 98 Dynamo Dresden Holstein Kiel How does the draw work? As in the second round, there will be no seeded teams in the round of 16 , meaning the biggest clubs could be drawn against each other. The team drawn first in each tie will play at home. When is the draw? The draw will take place on Sunday at 19:15 CET , when the Red Bulls will discover their opponents in the round of 16. item.title: ESPN legend tells Pat McAfee ‘not everybody is going to like you’ as controversy escalates
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Pat McAfee is enduring a rough period in his broadcasting career with threats putting his presence at this weekend’s college football show for ESPN under scrutiny. The former Indianapolis Colts punter has made a life for himself after football in the media as one of ESPN’s biggest earners. It is believed that only Stephen A. Smith who brings home more than McAfee following his rise inside the network. However, McAfee’s increased presence across ESPN’s shows has led to some frustration from certain fans who feel as if he is being pushed too hard by the network. There have even been some seriously concerning messages sent to the presenter online. As McAfee’s recent College GameDay visit to Utah has come under scrutiny, former ESPN anchor Linda Cohn has hit back at the 39-year-old. Former ESPN anchor hits back at Pat McAfee amid ESPN controversy Following his visit to Utah, McAfee shared his concerns for his own safety after the University’s own social media page shared a video calling him out ahead of his appearance. McAfee went on to say he ‘hated’ his visit to Utah which has seen even more people hitting out at the presenter. “Pat, why are you making sure the entire country sees the video that bothered you?” Cohn said on her YouTube channel. “A few college students make fun of you, you don’t like it, and your response gives those students a national audience they could never ever have reached themselves.” “By now, you have to know not everybody is going to like you. That’s the business. And some of those people, some of them are going to be college kids with an iPhone camera.” McAfee has certainly become a divisive figure for a lot of fans across the nation due to his outgoing personality and increased presence across ESPN’s products. However, it is clear to see here that he felt incredibly uncomfortable during his visit to Utah. item.title: ‘There’s a 50-50 Chance’ — Troy Aikman Drops Bombshell on Broadcasting Future Amid ESPN Contract Drama, Cowboys Front Office Rumors
item.description: ‘There’s a 50-50 Chance’ — Troy Aikman Drops Bombshell on Broadcasting Future Amid ESPN Contract Drama, Cowboys Front Office Rumors Troy Aikman could be approaching a career crossroads, with his future in the broadcast booth uncertain and a potential return to the Dallas Cowboys widely speculated. The Hall of Fame quarterback has yet to secure a new contract with ESPN, even as longtime partner Joe Buck has committed to the network for another six years. With Aikman approaching free agency, he offered his clearest indication yet that he may walk away from television after the 2026 NFL season, while leaving the door open to a possible reunion with Cowboys owner Jerry Jones. Troy Aikman Makes Major Admission About His Future as ESPN Contract Nears Expiration Aikman’s future with ESPN remains uncertain as his current contract is set to expire after Super Bowl 61, in March 2027. Despite continuing to call Monday Night Football alongside Buck, the former Cowboys quarterback has said the network has not formally approached him about negotiating a new deal. Aikman addressed the uncertainty Wednesday night at an event in Dallas, where he appeared alongside veteran sports journalist Peter King to discuss King’s new book, The Game. When asked whether he expected to continue calling NFL games in 2027, Aikman gave an uncertain answer, according to Dallas sports journalist Tim Cowlishaw. “I would say there’s a 50-50 chance,” Aikman said. With Aikman’s future at ESPN still unresolved, other networks could potentially become part of the conversation. CBS has already installed J.J. Watt as its lead analyst following Tony Romo’s departure. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer The network announced a new multiyear agreement for Watt last week. That leaves fewer obvious opportunities for Aikman to move directly into another major network’s top broadcast booth. Could Troy Aikman Return to the Dallas Cowboys? Meanwhile, Aikman’s relationship with the Dallas Cowboys has also attracted attention. Before calling Dallas’ win over the Philadelphia Eagles on ESPN’s Monday Night Football this week, the former Cowboys quarterback had an extended conversation with team owner Jerry Jones. Their interaction has fueled discussion about whether Aikman could eventually return to the franchise in a different capacity. Aikman has recently indicated that he would be open to exploring opportunities with the Cowboys. Speaking with Cowboys insider Mike Fisher, he acknowledged that his position had changed and that he was now willing to consider a potential role with the franchise. “Our relationship is complicated,” Aikman said on Fisher’s podcast. “I think he would agree with that. But it is one that’s built, I believe, on respect. This week, he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly. So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry.” “And quite honestly, I don’t know if there would be, or if there ever would be, an opportunity. But

item.title: ‘Drawing a blank’ – Robert Saleh seemingly forgets motivational speech for Titans in awkward clip
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Robert Saleh was speaking to reporters and describing what he said to the Tennessee Titans before he completely lost his train of thought. Saleh has been under the microscope ever since he took over as head coach of the Titans, following a second stint as the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers. The Titans have started the season 1-6 and have not looked great under Saleh. And his latest awkward moment during a press conference has only raised more questions about his fit as head coach. Robert Saleh loses his train of thought over Titans motivational talk during press conference Speaking to reporters ahead of the Tennessee Titans’ loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, HC Robert Saleh spoke about what he told the players as they continue to find their stride. While explaining his mindset to the reporters, Saleh began describing his message to the team, before immediately losing his train of thought. Saleh said: “We’ve just got to keep going through the process of learning how to finish. In the most extreme times, and this is what I told the team about today, and this is for all humans, not just football players. “In the most adverse moments, in the most pressure-packed moments, you’re always going to be… ummm… I’m drawing a blank. (to assistant coach) Do you remember what I said?” It was an awkward look for Saleh, who is already under pressure for not getting the most out of a young Titans team that many felt had a lot of potential coming into the new season. It doesn’t help that Saleh’s previous stint as head coach of the New York Jets ended disastrously, as management let him go for failing to get the best out of Aaron Rodgers and a strong offensive unit early into the 2024 season. Saleh has been under the microscope ever since he took over as head coach of the Titans, following a second stint as the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers. The Titans have started the season 1-6 and have not looked great under Saleh. And his latest awkward moment during a press conference has only raised more questions about his fit as head coach. Robert Saleh loses his train of thought over Titans motivational talk during press conference Speaking to reporters ahead of the Tennessee Titans’ loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, HC Robert Saleh spoke about what he told the players as they continue to find their stride. While explaining his mindset to the reporters, Saleh began describing his message to the team, before immediately losing his train of thought. Saleh said: “We’ve just got to keep going through the process of learning how to finish. In the most extreme times, and this is what I told the team about today, and this is for all humans, not just football players. “In the most adverse moments, in the most pressure-packed moments, you’re always going to be… ummm… I’m drawing a blank. (to assistant coach) Do you remember what I said?” It was an awkward look for Saleh, who is already under pressure for not getting the most out of a young Titans team that many felt had a lot of potential coming into the new season. item.title: New Episode of BBOC: Syracuse University Director of Athletics Bryan Blair
item.description: New Episode of BBOC: Syracuse University Director of Athletics Bryan Blair On the latest episode of JohnWallStreet Presents: Big Business on Campus , a college sports podcast powered by Playfly Sports, JohnWallStreet Founder Corey Leff and Playfly Sports Chairman Michael Schreiber sit down with Syracuse University Director of Athletics Bryan Blair. In this 40-minute conversation, the trio discuss: Treating Fundraising as a Math Equation Funding necessary venue upgrades, roster improvements and competitive coaching salaries will require Syracuse to first build out its philanthropic operation. “The secret sauce of fundraising is not [having] the flashiest suit, it is not [being] the smoothest talker. It's activity. And you [increase activity levels] one, by increasing bodies, [and] two, [by keeping] a focus on the [outreach]. ...Then it turns into a math equation. I need to raise this much, so that means I need to ask this many times of this many people with this much capacity,” Blair said. “ It takes a little bit of expense to [grow]. Sometimes people don't want to hear that, and in college athletics, we sometimes try to cut our way to prosperity. You can't do that and make the jumps that we need to make. So [we’re going] to invest. [We’ve] got to be willing to take some risks and know that [we’ve] pre-given the right amount of rigor to [fundraising to] make those dreams come true.” Central New York’s Renaissance Creating a Premium Growth Opportunity for SU Premium seating remains one of Syracuse University’s largest untapped commercial opportunities. Just 3%-4% of the Dome’s seats are currently tied to a suite or club experience. However, the region’s anticipated population growth and expanding business base would seemingly support increasing that share to 15%-20%. “This market just got the largest investment in the United States from Micron [Technology], $100 billion [to construct] semiconductor facilities. There's a waterfall of businesses moving to Central New York and we plan on having 100,000-150,000 more people in our population over the next five to 10 years. [There is] a massive renaissance [underway here]. Some are comparing it to the Erie Canal in terms of what it'll mean for this region,” Blair said. “So, [we’re trying to think about] how do we not only build a department that can be successful now, but skate to where the puck is going. Just 3%-4% of the Dome’s seats are currently tied to a suite or club experience. However, the region’s anticipated population growth and expanding business base would seemingly support increasing that share to 15%-20%. “This market just got the largest investment in the United States from Micron [Technology], $100 billion [to construct] semiconductor facilities. There's a waterfall of businesses moving to Central New York and we plan on having 100,000-150,000 more people in our population over the next five to 10 years. [There is] a massive renaissance [underway here]. Some are comparing it to the Erie Canal in terms of what it'll mean for this region,” Blair said. “So, [we’re trying to think about] how do we not only build a department that can be successful now, but skate to where the puck is going. How do we make this a place where they want to live, work, and play to that degree?” Youth Sports Being a Revenue Stream, NIL Vehicle and Fan Pipeline Blair launched the first youth sports league operated by a Division I athletic department during his time at Toledo. He sees an opportunity to replicate that model at Syracuse. “ Getting youth onto our campus and turning them into Toledo Rockets fans from an early age benefited our entire [University]. Toledo had some enrollment challenges, [and] we had lots of space in terms of fields and facilities that were not being used 365. We [also] had student athletes that [sought] NIL [income] and were willing to lean in and be coaches or assistant coaches or refs. So, you combine all of that and [we realized there was an opportunity to do well by doing good],” Blair said. “ But there [was also] a clear revenue component [to the initiative]. At Toledo, [youth sports became] a clear six-figure revenue driver [for us], which [still] had significant upside because we hadn't even [gotten around] to thinking about concessions and parking. We [also just started] pulling the data from registrants and the plan was to [eventually] feed that into the [ticketing funnel] in terms of giving participants free tickets, [while] mom, dad, [siblings], whoever [paid] to come to our games. There's just a [different] way to think about youth sports. [We’re going to] lean into [it here because] there's a lot of money in the ecosystem. There's a lot of brand equity in that ecosystem, and it's not a terribly heavy lift.” 📺 Watch the full video on JohnWallStreet’s YouTube Page . 🎧 Listen on Apple Podcasts or Spotify . item.title: Matrix takes sovereign messaging into the realm of the tech giants
item.description: Decentralized messaging platform Matrix is no longer the upstart it once was. The organization is now a serious challenger to the status quo as concerns about sovereignty and independence reach new heights. At the organization's recent Malmo event, which grew attendance 30 percent year-on-year, the mood shifted from "yes, this is important" to "yes, we're rolling this out." Matrix is an open standard for communication. It's a federated system, so there are no central hubs or overseas control to worry about, and it can be used for anything from messaging to voice over IP. Video is also supported. The system is an alternative to services such as Microsoft Teams. It has become popular in the public sector as governments grow increasingly wary of relying on US tech giants for services that the Trump administration could switch off at will . However, that increased interest and subsequent roll-outs have brought a level of scrutiny Matrix was not fully prepared for. A recent report regarding anonymous reaction to a roll-out of the technology by the European Commission took Element - the company that puts the lion share of the money into Matrix - by surprise. One attendee at the Malmo conference observed, "First they [competitors] ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you." Matrix remains an open standard, however, the open source foundation behind it would certainly welcome more paying members. "It's true that we're definitely getting more attention than we have had before," said Element CEO Matthew Hodgson. "We are seeing Matrix ending up on the critical path of digital sovereignty as almost the poster child of the whole thing. "I'm not sure that we necessarily do want to be the poster child," he added, "We didn't sign up to end up being ambassadors for digital sovereignty, roaming from government to government, but empirically that's where we've ended up, and yeah, that's going to attract attention from people who would rather everyone just kept in their traditional big tech systems." This comes amid worries about the reliability of international partners, from early projects including France's Tchap messenger for the public sector and Germany's BundesMessenger through to more recent users, such as the Swedish public sector. Indeed, in one memorable demonstration during the Matrix event, messages were sent between French, Swedish, and NATO entities. "I cannot overstate the strangeness," Hodgson added, "of having various national militaries phoning up every couple of days, saying, 'Look, we need to get on board Matrix too because we need to talk to this country and they're using Matrix, and we need to talk to that country, and they're using Matrix.'" "It could be for defense, could be national security, could just be healthcare or education, public sector. But that is real. That is why there is a feeding frenzy." item.content:encoded: Decentralized messaging platform Matrix is no longer the upstart it once was. The organization is now a serious challenger to the status quo as concerns about sovereignty and independence reach new heights. At the organization's recent Malmo event, which grew attendance 30 percent year-on-year, the mood shifted from "yes, this is important" to "yes, we're rolling this out." Matrix is an open standard for communication. It's a federated system, so there are no central hubs or overseas control to worry about, and it can be used for anything from messaging to voice over IP. Video is also supported. The system is an alternative to services such as Microsoft Teams. It has become popular in the public sector as governments grow increasingly wary of relying on US tech giants for services that the Trump administration could switch off at will . However, that increased interest and subsequent roll-outs have brought a level of scrutiny Matrix was not fully prepared for. A recent report regarding anonymous reaction to a roll-out of the technology by the European Commission took Element - the company that puts the lion share of the money into Matrix - by surprise. One attendee at the Malmo conference observed, "First they [competitors] ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you." Matrix remains an open standard, however, the open source foundation behind it would certainly welcome more paying members. "It's true that we're definitely getting more attention than we have had before," said Element CEO Matthew Hodgson. "We are seeing Matrix ending up on the critical path of digital sovereignty as almost the poster child of the whole thing. "I'm not sure that we necessarily do want to be the poster child," he added, "We didn't sign up to end up being ambassadors for digital sovereignty, roaming from government to government, but empirically that's where we've ended up, and yeah, that's going to attract attention from people who would rather everyone just kept in their traditional big tech systems." This comes amid worries about the reliability of international partners, from early projects including France's Tchap messenger for the public sector and Germany's BundesMessenger through to more recent users, such as the Swedish public sector. Indeed, in one memorable demonstration during the Matrix event, messages were sent between French, Swedish, and NATO entities. "I cannot overstate the strangeness," Hodgson added, "of having various national militaries phoning up every couple of days, saying, 'Look, we need to get on board Matrix too because we need to talk to this country and they're using Matrix, and we need to talk to that country, and they're using Matrix.'" "It could be for defense, could be national security, could just be healthcare or education, public sector. But that is real. That is why there is a feeding frenzy." Not that Element or Matrix is trying to build a better Teams than Teams. Patrick Alberts, Element's Chief Product Officer, said, "This is a digitally sovereign communication solution that, by and large, works like Teams in many aspects, but it's not set out to be the faster Porsche here..." As for the reported complaints from the European Commission over Element's software implementation, Diana Gheorghe, EC head of sector for Communication and Collaboration Services, addressed them directly and described the anonymous complaints as "the natural friction of [a] high-profile rollout that we have done at scale." Alexandru Vignide, EC service manager for Communication and Collaboration Services, who is very much at the pointy end of making the sovereign communication tools work, noted the speed of the rollout, which began with a proof of concept in Q4 2025, and hit laptops between July and September 2026. The EC chose the Schengen Cloud Alliance (which includes OVHcloud) for hosting and, according to Vignide, "We wanted to provide a familiar experience for users." Not everyone is impressed with what is rolling out , but it's important to remember that change can be alarming, and this is still early days. It is, however, a significant one. Gheorghe said that, as well as increasing resilience and business continuity, "We wanted to have vendor diversity. We also wanted to have data control and ownership of the platform." Microsoft, as an example, would point to the sovereign capabilities of its system. As the Matrix conference kicked off, it announced new capabilities , including additional options for running AI, data services, and confidential workloads on customer-controlled platforms, and highlighted its sovereign partner ecosystem for customers who prefer local expertise. However, Microsoft (and other tech giants) cannot escape concerns about who ultimately controls the data and what administrations might do with it. In 2025, a Microsoft representative memorably confirmed the US giant " cannot guarantee " data sovereignty to customers in France. There is, however, a fly in the Matrix ointment. The platform is open source and, like so many open source projects, requires funding. Right now, Element accounts for much of the Matrix Foundation's funding. Hodgson finds this a little frustrating. "If every government who is operationally dependent on Matrix put the smallest amount of money in the Foundation, the Foundation would have enough money to really start investing in the ecosystem and not be dependent on Element basically picking up the tab." He acknowledged that things had improved in the last year, but said, "It's not good governance for an open standard to have one big player like Element effectively propping things up." This isn't uncommon in the open source world , and it's a little disappointing given the ever-increasing importance placed on sovereignty in communications. Alberts commented: "There is confusion in the market that the thing somehow creates itself. "No, it doesn't. It requires hardworking people. These hardworking people need to be paid, and that payment, in order to support government deployments going forward, ideally also comes from these governments. And some of them do a lot and do it in a great way, and that's amazing. "But some don't." ®

item.title: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter
item.description: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter Manchester United travel to West London to take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime. The Red Devils have faced off against the Blues 199 times , meaning this match will be the 200th competitive game between the two rivals. United have come out on top 85 times in history, with Chelsea winning 57. There have also been 57 draws during the storied fixture. Here are three storylines to get the blood pumping. United closing in on unwanted record After Michael Carrick’s side lost 0-3 at home to AFC Bournemouth last Sunday, they had officially gone six Premier League matches without a win. This is already the second-longest winless streak in their Premier League history. The longest arrived in May 2025 when they went eight matches without a win. Nonetheless, with matches against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool to come, it is not exactly clear where the next win will come from. United are still some way off their worst ever run, not winning in 16 consecutive matches way back in the 1929-1930 season. Chelsea record Fortunately, the Red Devils have quite a respectable record as of late against Saturday’s opponents. In their last ten matches against the Blues, they have only lost twice. There have been four United wins, including two last season, and four draws since 2021. Former players Man United and Chelsea have had a lot of former players play for one another over the years. Andrey Santos has not had the best start to his United career, but he moved from Chelsea in the summer and, with Kobbie Mainoo still out, he will likely get another chance to start in the midfield against his former team. One player United will not want to face is their former player Danny Welbeck. The Carrington youth product moved to Stamford Bridge in the summer and has haunted United many times in the past, scoring six times against them for Brighton and Arsenal.

item.title: Iraola praises Liverpool teenager after man-of-the-match Chelsea performance
item.description: Iraola praises Liverpool teenager after man-of-the-match Chelsea performance Andoni Iraola praised the performance of Trey Nyoni after the Liverpool midfielder was named man of the match during the club’s Carabao Cup win over Chelsea. Liverpool reached the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after beating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties at Anfield, following a 1-1 draw in normal time. Iraola opted to rotate his team for the clash, ahead of a Premier League meeting with Arsenal this weekend, and handed Nyoni a start in central midfield. The 19-year-old has been on the fringes of the first team this season and impressed, earning the Player of the Match award from Liverpool’s official social media channels. Iraola said Nyoni did ‘very well’ and was pleased how his youngsters handled the occasion, with academy graduate Lewis Koumas also starting against Chelsea. “I think he has done very well. Really well. It’s good for the young players especially to live these experiences in cup competitions, where if you lose you are out,” Iraola said in his post-match press conference. “We have been losing and then the draw. Then they haven’t been there in the penalty shootout but they lived the feelings. They played under pressure against a very good team. And Trey has finished physically in a good place, so well done, yes.” Ballon d’Or 2026 – Every winner from this year’s ceremony See Also – Five of the best Premier League away kits in 2026/27 Follow the Football Faithful on Social Media: Facebook | Instagram | Twitter | YouTube | TikTok

item.title: South Korea boss backs Son as captain after rift rumours
item.description: Son Heung-min has been called up by South Korea for friendlies next month against Saudi Arabia and Qatar (Philip FONG) Son Heung-min will continue as South Korea captain despite reports of friction between the former Tottenham striker and his senior international team-mates, coach Robert Moreno said Thursday. Moreno named Son, now 34 and playing for LAFC in Major League Soccer, in his squad for friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Qatar next month. He also selected experienced Europe-based trio Kim Min-jae, Hwang Hee-chan and Hwang In-beom, who reports say were ready to quit the national team last month. Moreno said he had held "many conversations with the players" since taking over on an interim basis after South Korea's World Cup flop in North America. "I spent more time communicating than training," the Spaniard said at a press conference that lasted more than an hour. "Even in the best teams people can have different opinions. What matters is how those differences are resolved." Moreno's contract is set to expire after the two friendlies, although South Korean football chiefs could keep him on for the Asian Cup, scheduled for Saudi Arabia in January. When asked about Son's leadership role in the team, Moreno said: "The captain is Son Heung-min. I have nothing more to say." Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of a 0-0 home friendly draw with Venezuela this month. Kim said afterwards that "every player needs to put their head down and give it their all", fuelling talk of divisions within the squad. Moreno said "the team is healthy" and backed the players to work together. "I believe you can find the answer in what I have said today and the squad that has been announced," he said. South Korea's football association this month told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks" on players. The national team is in the crosshairs after a poor showing at the World Cup, which saw coach Hong Myung-bo quit after they failed to get past the group stage. amk/pst

item.title: Bearman Has Scored 23 of Haas’s 30 Points. Now He Reportedly Wants $6.7 Million
item.description: Oliver Bearman has scored 23 of Haas’s 30 points in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and he reportedly wants to be paid like it: €6 million, about $6.7 million, a year to stay with the team. The figure comes from F1 business writer Marc Limacher, as Read Motorsport reported . Haas is reportedly unwilling to pay it, which has slowed talks on a 2027 deal, as we reported this week . Neither Bearman nor Haas has confirmed the number. What Bearman Is Paid Now RacingNews365’s estimates of 2026 base salaries put Bearman on about $1 million, among the lowest on the grid. Teams don’t publish contracts, and the estimates leave out bonuses and personal sponsorship, according to RacingNews365 . Here’s how that compares with points scored after 18 rounds: Driver Team Estimated 2026 salary 2026 points Max Verstappen Red Bull $70 million 236 Lewis Hamilton Ferrari $60 million 241 Esteban Ocon Haas $7 million 7 Isack Hadjar Red Bull $5 million 105 Kimi Antonelli Mercedes $2 million 365 Oliver Bearman Haas $1 million 23 Liam Lawson Racing Bulls $1 million 77 The raise Bearman is reportedly asking for would put him at about what his teammate is estimated to earn. Ocon, who leaves Haas after this season, has 7 points. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has won nine Grands Prix on an estimated $2 million. Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid on Sept. 12, 2026. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) Why Bearman Says It’s Out of His Hands Haas has already confirmed Ferrari junior Rafael Cámara as Ocon’s replacement for 2027, but it hasn’t confirmed Bearman alongside him. Both sides say they want to keep going. “I think on our side as well, if I’m not mistaken, we’re very sure that we want to continue working together, and the only sticking points are kind of out of my hands, more contractual points,” Bearman told reporters at the US Grand Prix. He’s also a Ferrari junior, and he made it clear Haas isn’t where he plans to end up. “In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with, and I see my future with,” he said. “But at some point, as well, I feel like I’ve earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top four team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal.” For now, Ferrari has Charles Leclerc on a long-term deal and Lewis Hamilton in the other seat. Haas is seventh in the constructors’ standings with 30 points, and Bearman’s 23 points put him 13th in the drivers’ championship. The next race is the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, Nov. 1, the next chance for either side to say where the talks stand.
item.content:encoded: Oliver Bearman has scored 23 of Haas’s 30 points in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and he reportedly wants to be paid like it: €6 million, about $6.7 million, a year to stay with the team. The figure comes from F1 business writer Marc Limacher, as Read Motorsport reported . Haas is reportedly unwilling to pay it, which has slowed talks on a 2027 deal, as we reported this week . Neither Bearman nor Haas has confirmed the number. What Bearman Is Paid Now RacingNews365’s estimates of 2026 base salaries put Bearman on about $1 million, among the lowest on the grid. Teams don’t publish contracts, and the estimates leave out bonuses and personal sponsorship, according to RacingNews365 . item.title: Chelsea injury nightmare deepens as Xabi Alonso provides update on Maxence Lacroix blow against Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Chelsea’s injury problems have gone from bad to worse after Maxence Lacroix was forced to withdraw during their Carabao Cup showdown against Liverpool. The French defender appeared to suffer a hamstring issue during the first half at Anfield, adding further strain to Xabi Alonso’s already depleted squad. Lacroix limps off at Anfield The Blues crashed out of the Carabao Cup following a tense penalty shootout, with normal time ending 1-1 after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo traded spot-kicks. However, the loss of their commanding centre-back will be of far greater concern to the Chelsea coaching staff. Lacroix pulled up while chasing Gakpo through midfield shortly after Liverpool's equaliser. He went down off the ball moments later and required treatment on the pitch before being replaced by Levi Colwill. The Frenchman walked slowly to the dressing room in clear distress, clutching the back of his left thigh while consulting with the club's medical trainers. Alonso reacts to fresh fitness setback Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted the club will have to wait before discovering the full extent of the defender's muscle issue. Speaking after the final whistle, the Spaniard confirmed the medical team's initial suspicions. "Too early to tell. Probably he felt something on the hamstrings," Alonso said. "And we need a couple of days to check what's going to be the injury.” Mounting problems at Stamford Bridge Losing Lacroix represents a massive blow to Chelsea's defensive stability. The summer signing from Crystal Palace has been an ever-present figure this season, starting all eight Premier League fixtures and featuring in both Carabao Cup matches. His absence exacerbates an already severe selection crisis for Alonso. The west London outfit travelled north without Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, and Reece James due to injury, while talisman Cole Palmer missed the tie through suspension. Waiting game for the Blues Chelsea's medical staff will assess Lacroix over the coming days to determine a precise recovery timeline. A prolonged absence would stretch the squad to its limits, leaving Alonso heavily reliant on Colwill and his remaining defensive options during a busy autumn schedule. The manager must now regroup his depleted squad as they look to shake off their cup elimination and maintain momentum in the Premier League.

item.title: Google Pay Now Available to Visa Card Holders in Nigeria for Fast, Secure Digital Payments
item.description: Visa , one of the world’s leaders in digital payments, applauds the launch of Google Pay by participating financial institutions in Nigeria, supported through Visa’s partnership with Google . Eligible Visa cardholders of participating financial institutions can now securely add their cards to Google Wallet and make fast, convenient, and secure payments across millions of contactless acceptance points and online merchants. The launch by participating financial institutions marks another significant milestone in Nigeria’s digital payments journey, providing consumers with a simple and secure way to pay using their Android devices. By adding their eligible Visa cards to Google Wallet, users can tap to pay in stores, make purchases online, and enjoy a seamless payment experience across Google’s ecosystem. Google Pay uses tokenization technology to help protect payment information. Instead of storing or sharing a customer’s card number during transactions, a unique digital token is used, providing an additional layer of security while maintaining a fast and convenient checkout experience. As consumer demand for digital-first payment experiences continues to grow, the partnership between Visa and Google, working alongside Nigerian financial institutions, aims to support contactless payment adoption and provide Nigerians with more ways to pay securely wherever Visa contactless payments are accepted. “At Visa, we are committed to advancing the future of payments by delivering innovative, secure, and seamless payment experiences for consumers across Nigeria and beyond . Through our partnership with Google, we are pleased to support our financial institution partners as they bring Google Pay to their cardholders, combining the security of Visa’s global payment network with the convenience consumers increasingly expect in a digital-first world. Helping more people pay with confidence using their mobile devices supports digital commerce, financial inclusion, and the continued growth of Nigeria’s digital economy,” said Andrew Uaboi , Vice President and Cluster Head, Visa West Africa . “We are delighted to bring Google Wallet to Nigeria, a market at the forefront of financial innovation in Africa. Google Wallet makes everyday transactions faster and safer while removing the friction of carrying physical cards. By working alongside Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, we are expanding access to modern digital payment tools for millions of everyday consumers,” said Olumide Balogun , Country Director, Google West Africa About Visa Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable, and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses, and economies to thrive. item.title: Tinubu To Induct Five Helicopters Acquired By NAF
item.description: As part of efforts to sustain the fight against insecurity, President Bola Tinubu is set to induct five new helicopters acquired by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF). The helicopters, made up of two Airbus H-125 and three Agusta 109 Trekker B, will be inducted at the newly reconstructed hangar of the NAF at the presidential wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja. President Tinubu is also expected to commission the newly reconstructed hangar housing the helicopters. NAF took delivery of the new helicopters last month as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to confront evolving security threats. The newly acquired platforms comprise three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters manufactured by Leonardo Helicopters of Italy and two H-125 helicopters produced by Airbus Helicopters. A statement by the NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the acquisition was part of the Federal Government’s sustained investment in strengthening the operational capabilities of the service. Ejodame said the three AW-109 Trekker B helicopters arrived in Lagos on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, as part of a batch of 10 recently acquired by the Federal Government. He said the remaining seven helicopters were expected to be delivered before the end of 2026. The two H-125 helicopters had earlier been delivered to the NAF, bringing the total number of helicopters covered by the latest acquisition to five. The post Tinubu To Induct Five Helicopters Acquired By NAF appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Allied People’s Movement, APM, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to disclose his actual destination, insisting that he should remain in Nigeria to pray for the country and tackle the hardship facing citizens. The party argued that Tinubu should address Nigeria’s mounting problems at home rather than embark on a trip, it questioned, alleging that the announced lesser Hajj pilgrimage should not serve as a cover for other activities. In a statement, APM National Publicity Secretary Abubakar Yusuf questioned the purpose of the President’s trip, insisting that the pilgrimage should not be used to distract from the challenges confronting Nigerians. “Lesser Hajj involves prayer and supplications, but not an opportunity to do the unusual or as a cover to do other things,” Yusuf said. Accusing Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship in the country, the APM spokesman said the president should stay back and address the problems facing ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot pray for the problems you have inflicted on ordinary Nigerians, rather than staying here to resolve the heavily burdened, self-contrived problems of the citizens,” he said. Yusuf also invoked the popular ‘Andrew, check out’ expression, urging Tinubu not to leave the country. “Let Mr President not behave like ‘Andrew’ of those days, saying President Bola Ahmed Tinubu should not check out,” he said. Looking ahead to the 2027 presidential election, Yusuf claimed Tinubu could struggle to secure the required 25 per cent of votes in 12 selected states, challenging the president to pay attention to his electoral prospects. The APM spokesman expressed confidence that the party’s presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, would defeat Tinubu in 2027, describing him as a workaholic and energetic contender poised to challenge the President’s political dominance in the South-West and across the South. The post Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘This abuse must end’ – Sowore reacts to remand of Doris Ogala
item.description: Human rights activist, Omoyele Sowore, has condemned the remand of actress Doris Ogala at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the hearing and determination of her bail application over alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor. Ogala was arraigned Wednesday on three counts by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation before Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos on allegations bordering on the publication of intimate photographs, dissemination of allegedly false electronic messages and threats against the cleric. The prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, told the court that between September 2024 and March 2026, Ogala published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent. He alleged that the publication was capable of causing annoyance, embarrassment, emotional distress and injury to the cleric’s reputation. In his reaction on Facebook, Sowore accused the police of weaponising the Cybercrimes Act to serve the interest of “influential figures”. “Once again, the Nigeria Police Force has deepened its weaponization of the Cybercrimes Act! What kind of society are we becoming? How could anyone be arraigned simply over allegations of having an affair with a pastor? And how could the police actually take such a matter before a Federal High Court judge? “Even more troubling is that the case has reportedly been brought before Justice Aluko of the Federal High Court in Lagos, a judge whose handling of cases involving pastors raises serious concerns about judicial impartiality. The perception that the police and judiciary are being used to settle personal scores and protect influential religious figures must be confronted. “The Nigeria Police Force has no business turning private relationships into criminal prosecutions or deploying the Cybercrimes Act as a weapon of intimidation,” he wrote. Sowore noted that Ogala, as the governorship candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) in Abia State, deserves the full protection of her constitutional rights, due process, and a fair hearing. “The police must stop criminalizing private disputes, and the judiciary must never become an instrument of religious influence or personal vendettas. This abuse must end!” he added. Ogala’s case was adjourned until October 30, 2026, for the hearing of her bail application. The post ‘This abuse must end’ – Sowore reacts to remand of Doris Ogala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Admin dropped the F-bomb in a password to show hackers who was really 1337
item.description: Welcome back to PWNED, in which The Reg offers cautionary tales from folks who’ve left their doors wide open to attackers and lived to tell the tale. This week’s misadventure involves unpatched older machines and a password that was supposed to send a message to crims. Our story comes courtesy once again of leading red teamer and pen tester Dahvid Schloss of Suzu Labs . A client asked Schloss to visit a factory and check the servers there for security holes. The company had been hacked six months prior, made some adjustments, and wanted to make sure that they were bulletproof now. Schloss' mission, which he chose to accept, was to get domain admin rights. Schloss drove over to the factory where he noticed a number of Windows 7 servers were connected to the CNC milling machines, even though Windows 10 was by then Microsoft's supported desktop OS. This was to be expected, as companies with proprietary software often use legacy OSes for fear of breaking apps. At first, Schloss had a hard time breaking in because most of the servers were not connected to the domain. So there was no point in his running the EternalBlue zero-day that would have let him in. “So I've been looking through these and most of them had been disconnected from the domain, so it's the right move,” he said. “Like, yeah, you could run EternalBlue on the network, but you really weren't going to be able to get anywhere with it, cuz you get on the device and what you find: you dump LSASS [the Windows Local Security Authority Subsystem Service], you’re like ‘All right, there’s local admin creds, but the local admin creds on those devices were different from the local admin creds on the majority of workstations.” Finally, Schloss went onto one of the servers that was connected to milling machines and found that it was connected to the network and on the domain. It was vulnerable to EternalBlue and he went and dumped LSASS and found a pair of creds from WDigest, one of which looked like an admin account. But Schloss thought that it must not be a legitimate admin account when he read the password : “heyhackergof***yourself,” but written in leet speak [ l337 5p34k ]. The resulting string was a strong password, but Schloss assumed that the admins were playing a game with him and left this credential there for him to find. Schloss assumed it wouldn't work and sat on it for a week. During a briefing he had with the IT crew, he presented his findings and then asked who set up the admin account with this funny password. “You could see everyone kind of looking at the senior manager of IT like ‘that was you, wasn’t it,’” Schloss explained. “He’s kind of got this face. I’m like ‘oh shit, like what?’ Turns out that ‘heyhackergof***yourself’ was the actual password for his admin account." On Monday, Schloss tried the username and password combo and, lo and behold, it gave him complete control of the entire network. He was then able to get access to other passwords and many of them were also insults

This week’s misadventure involves unpatched older machines and a password that was supposed to send a message to crims. Our story comes courtesy once again of leading red teamer and pen tester Dahvid Schloss of Suzu Labs . A client asked Schloss to visit a factory and check the servers there for security holes. Schloss' mission, which he chose to accept, was to get domain admin rights. Schloss drove over to the factory where he noticed a number of Windows 7 servers were connected to the CNC milling machines, even though Windows 10 was by then Microsoft's supported desktop OS. This was to be expected, as companies with proprietary software often use legacy OSes for fear of breaking apps. At first, Schloss had a hard time breaking in because most of the servers were not connected to the domain. So there was no point in his running the EternalBlue zero-day that would have let him in. “So I've been looking through these and most of them had been disconnected from the domain, so it's the right move,” he said. “Like, yeah, you could run EternalBlue on the network, but you really weren't going to be able to get anywhere with it, cuz you get on the device and what you find: you dump LSASS [the Windows Local Security Authority Subsystem Service], you’re like ‘All right, there’s local admin creds, but the local admin creds on those devices were different from the local admin creds on the majority of workstations.” Finally, Schloss went onto one of the servers that was connected to milling machines and found that it was connected to the network and on the domain. It was vulnerable to EternalBlue and he went and dumped LSASS and found a pair of creds from WDigest, one of which looked like an admin account. But Schloss thought that it must not be a legitimate admin account when he read the password : “heyhackergof***yourself,” but written in leet speak [ l337 5p34k ]. The resulting string was a strong password, but Schloss assumed that the admins were playing a game with him and left this credential there for him to find. Schloss assumed it wouldn't work and sat on it for a week. During a briefing he had with the IT crew, he presented his findings and then asked who set up the admin account with this funny password. “You could see everyone kind of looking at the senior manager of IT like ‘that was you, wasn’t it,’” Schloss explained. “He’s kind of got this face. I’m like ‘oh shit, like what?’ Turns out that ‘heyhackergof***yourself’ was the actual password for his admin account." On Monday, Schloss tried the username and password combo and, lo and behold, it gave him complete control of the entire network. He was then able to get access to other passwords and many of them were also insults directed at potential hackers. Schloss understood that the team was still angry about a breach they had suffered six months prior and, should they be breached again, wanted to give the finger to the hacker who did it. Unfortunately, their system was still vulnerable because of the outdated machine that was hooked up to the domain and he was able to gain control. The lesson here is really to patch your systems and avoid using insecure legacy OSes whenever possible, because it was an old machine that let Schloss in, not a weak password. Indeed, “hackergof***yourself” in leet speak isn’t a terrible password, just an embarrassing one if it's exposed. ®

item.title: HPE puts storage to work on AI’s expensive memory problem
item.description: HPE is giving its Alletra Storage MP X10000 another job: holding inference state that would otherwise be evicted from expensive GPU memory and recalculated later. In testing validated by Kamiwaza using NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the Kamiwaza AI platform, and HPE Alletra MP X10000, the solution achieved up to 20× faster time to first token and 17× higher effective inference throughput versus running without KV cache offload. The GPUs did not become cleverer. They had less repeat work to do. The results move a storage decision directly into the discussion about AI economics. Model pricing gets plenty of attention. Paying expensive accelerators to process the same context repeatedly deserves some too. Especially as enterprises move from chatbots answering individual questions to agents that can turn one request into a small committee’s worth of activity. Your agents have a repetition problem Agentic workflows repeatedly process documents, system instructions and conversation histories. One agent retrieves information, another evaluates it, a third checks the result, and subsequent steps revisit material the system has already processed. Some repetition is necessary. Recalculating everything is not. KV cache retains intermediate attention state, allowing compatible requests to reuse earlier computation. Keeping that cache available can reduce the work required before a model starts producing its next answer. GPU memory, unfortunately, is neither infinite nor priced as though it were. Long contexts and concurrent sessions compete for that memory. When reusable cache is evicted and later needed, the inference engine may have to rebuild it. More GPU work, more waiting, and no additional insight to show for either. HPE Alletra MP X10000 provides a shared tier for offloaded cache, while RDMA for S3 accelerates the storage data path. The proposition: retrieve reusable context rather than make the GPU calculate it again. Compute once. Reuse often. An unremarkable principle, until the alternative appears on the infrastructure bill. Twenty times faster, with the denominator attached The Kamiwaza-validated testing used NVIDIA Nemotron 70B and more than 30 concurrent agents under large-context, multi-agent inference. That matters because this is precisely the sort of real-world workload where repeated context and memory pressure can make cache reuse valuable. Several agents consulting overlapping material create a different opportunity from unrelated, short prompts with little context in common. Those headline gains are workload-specific. Context length, concurrency, cache hit rates and transfer overhead determine the return. Twenty times faster is a test result, not a universal entitlement. Buyers should examine the comparison as carefully as the multiplier: the same workload, with and without KV cache offload, and enough concurrency to represent production conditions. item.dc:creator: Colin Gallagher
item.content:encoded: HPE is giving its Alletra Storage MP X10000 another job: holding inference state that would otherwise be evicted from expensive GPU memory and recalculated later. In testing validated by Kamiwaza using NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the Kamiwaza AI platform, and HPE Alletra MP X10000, the solution achieved up to 20× faster time to first token and 17× higher effective inference throughput versus running without KV cache offload. The GPUs did not become cleverer. They had less repeat work to do. The results move a storage decision directly into the discussion about AI economics. Model pricing gets plenty of attention. Paying expensive accelerators to process the same context repeatedly deserves some too. Especially as enterprises move from chatbots answering individual questions to agents that can turn one request into a small committee’s worth of activity. Your agents have a repetition problem Agentic workflows repeatedly process documents, system instructions and conversation histories. One agent retrieves information, another evaluates it, a third checks the result, and subsequent steps revisit material the system has already processed. Some repetition is necessary. Recalculating everything is not. KV cache retains intermediate attention state, allowing compatible requests to reuse earlier computation. Keeping that cache available can reduce the work required before a model starts producing its next answer. GPU memory, unfortunately, is neither infinite nor priced as though it were. Long contexts and concurrent sessions compete for that memory. When reusable cache is evicted and later needed, the inference engine may have to rebuild it. More GPU work, more waiting, and no additional insight to show for either. HPE Alletra MP X10000 provides a shared tier for offloaded cache, while RDMA for S3 accelerates the storage data path. The proposition: retrieve reusable context rather than make the GPU calculate it again. Compute once. Reuse often. An unremarkable principle, until the alternative appears on the infrastructure bill. Twenty times faster, with the denominator attached The Kamiwaza-validated testing used NVIDIA Nemotron 70B and more than 30 concurrent agents under large-context, multi-agent inference. That matters because this is precisely the sort of real-world workload where repeated context and memory pressure can make cache reuse valuable. Several agents consulting overlapping material create a different opportunity from unrelated, short prompts with little context in common. Those headline gains are workload-specific. Context length, concurrency, cache hit rates and transfer overhead determine the return. Twenty times faster is a test result, not a universal entitlement. Buyers should examine the comparison as carefully as the multiplier: the same workload, with and without KV cache offload, and enough concurrency to represent production conditions. The useful question is how much repeated computation their applications can avoid, and whether retrieving cached context is faster than rebuilding it. A large performance number without its test conditions is mostly a typography decision. Garbage in still costs money Cache reuse addresses repeated computation. It cannot rescue a retrieval system that feeds the model half the company’s document archive to answer one question. HPE’s broader pitch pairs the X10000 with Data Fabric for governed access to distributed data. The X10000’s data intelligence node generates metadata, classification and embeddings at ingest to help applications retrieve relevant context. That moves preparation closer to where data lands, rather than leaving every application team to assemble another downstream preparation pipeline. The economic logic is straightforward. More precise retrieval can mean less irrelevant material in prompts and fewer attempts to obtain a useful answer. Enterprise archives are rarely short of documents. Distinguishing the current policy from six superseded versions and a presentation called “FINAL_final_v7” is the more interesting problem. Governance also matters when agents retrieve information and act on it. Relevant context still needs to be authorized context. Faster access to something an agent should never have seen is an awkward definition of progress. That gives HPE two economic levers: improve what enters inference, then reuse computation where possible. The distinction matters. Better retrieval can reduce prompt size and retries. KV cache reuse reduces processing work; it does not magically shrink generated answers or oblige an API supplier to lower its bill. Beyond the cache checkbox Cache offload is becoming a crowded market. HPE’s strength rests on combining it with data preparation and governance, rather than winning another feature tick. The practical test for organizations looking to get more value from their AI is how smoothly data preparation, governance and cache reuse operate as a single system. Can applications find relevant, permitted information without unnecessary copying and preparation? Can the inference engine retain and retrieve reusable context efficiently? Does the combination sustain useful throughput as context windows and agent counts grow? Those questions connect the architecture to observable outcomes. Buyers should ask for cache hit rates, time to first token and sustained throughput on their workloads. They should also examine retrieval quality and whether the system completes the intended task. A faster wrong answer remains a wrong answer, however attractive the benchmark chart. Cost per terabyte remains relevant. So does the cost of making a GPU read the same briefing for the seventh time. For more information, visit the HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000 web page . Contributed by HPE

item.title: Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China
item.description: Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won’t be easily or quickly repaired, experts say. The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao. Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”. Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China. He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing. Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV. Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said. China has the world’s second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised. A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously”. – ‘Serious damage’ – So is that the end of the matter? “Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP. “It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China. “In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high. “An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story. “It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.” The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale. Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters. NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said. The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year. NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year. Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case — and now Mbappe — an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”. NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split. – No way back? – Spanish football also has a lot to lose. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker’s comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won’t be easily or quickly repaired, experts say. The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao. Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”. Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People’s Republic of China. He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing. Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV. Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said. China has the world’s second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised. A spokesman for China’s foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe’s apology “seriously”. – ‘Serious damage’ – So is that the end of the matter? “Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident,” Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP. “It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China. “In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high. “An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story. “It’s better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it’s definitely not the end of the story.” The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale. Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters. NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said. The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year. NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year. Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case — and now Mbappe — an illustration of China’s consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into “a spiral of outrage”. NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the league lost “hundreds of millions of dollars” over the split. – No way back? – Spanish football also has a lot to lose. A source within La Liga told AFP that China and the United States alone finance the “majority” of international broadcasting rights, which were valued at 748 million euros ($834 million) for the 2024-25 season. According to the Real Madrid-affiliated newspaper Marca, the Madrid club generates between 10 and 15 percent of its sales of jerseys and merchandise in China. Real Madrid also counts Chinese companies among its main sponsors, with Hisense, sports betting firm Kaiyun Sports, and Linglong Tire all featuring prominently. Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said showing fast and heartfelt remorse was the first step. “This will influence the decision on whether to continue the broadcast ban and, if so, for how long,” he told AFP. Sports commentator Yan cast doubt on whether the reputation of Mbappe, whose face has adorned drinks bottles and advertising campaigns in China, can ever fully recover. “Judging by commercial sponsorships and big ad campaigns he appeared in during the World Cup, he has a huge influence in China,” he said. “If that influence can’t be sustained there can be no talk of commercial interests, and La Liga and Real Madrid will definitely be badly affected.” Yan said it was “genuinely hard to predict” what happens next. “In the short term, I’m certainly not optimistic,” he added. “If they want to repair their image and the relationship, their future actions and behaviour will be key.” The post Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down
item.description: From Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler. Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questions There is real tragedy in this week’s story of the three-year-old Florida boy whose parents claimed he was so good at soccer that police were called to do what opposing defenders couldn’t . But it doesn’t lie where the outrage cycle wants you to think. It’s broader, implicates more people, and to me, is far more depressing. You may have seen the video by now. Here was a toddler with fabulous soccer talent, running end-to-end and scoring goal after goal against opponents who have seemingly just found their feet. The cameraman, later identified as the child’s father, loudly and proudly cheers his son on. Way to go, kid. Continue reading...

item.title: Time and owners not on Moyes’ side as he tries to end Everton trophy drought
item.description: The Friedkin Group want to sell and squad investment has dried up but Carabao Cup is still an opportunity for silverware A European challenge plus a concerted effort to end a trophy drought that will soon stretch into a 32nd year were Everton’s stated aims for this season, although that was before the club’s owners turned the taps off in the transfer market and announced they were looking to sell up. An abrupt change of direction and ambition from The Friedkin Group (TFG) has not altered the demands on David Moyes, however. It is as you were for the Everton manager, regardless of the tools at his disposal. Newcastle’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Thursday – when they will be backed by 7,732 fans after Everton allocated their opponents 15% of the ground – is timely on several counts. It is, first and foremost, an opportunity for Moyes’s team to advance in a competition that Everton have never won and edge closer to realising one stated aim for the campaign. It is also a chance to restore positivity after consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal , Everton’s only losses of the season. Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham’s season has finally taken off. How far up the table can they go?
item.description: Spurs had an awful start but, after an impressive win at Chelsea, they are suddenly looking up at the table By Opta Analyst In reality, it was only three points. All Tottenham took from their 2-0 win at Chelsea last Saturday evening was a helpful boost in the Premier League standings. But it feels far more significant than that. This is a fixture Tottenham almost never win. In their 34 previous visits to Chelsea in the Premier League, they had won only once. It was their first win to nil at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986, nearly 40 years ago. Winning at Chelsea is huge. Plenty of Spurs fans have only ever seen this happen once before, in April 2018 under Mauricio Pochettino, when their team was a formidable force. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 Forgotten 'Peanuts' Characters That Charles Schulz Abandoned in the Comic Strip
item.description: Every long-running comic strip has a few characters who got phased out early on. The most famous example might be Lyman from Garfield , Jon's roommate and Odie's original owner, who simply disappeared one day around 1985. (Davis has occasionally joked that if you want to find Lyman, you should dig up Jon's basement.) You could also point to most of the early human characters in Bloom County , Nicole in Doonesbury getting sidelined in favor of Joanie Caucus, or the abortive Uncle Max arc in Calvin and Hobbes .
