item.title: This Underrated 5-Season Fantasy Series Is Basically Harry Potter for Adults
item.description: I think far too much about the first chapter of Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince , in which the outgoing and incoming Ministers of Magic meet the British prime minister at 10 Downing Street. A bridge has collapsed, and one of the PM’s junior ministers has started quacking like a duck. Truly nefarious stuff. The wizards explain that these and other disasters are connected to the return of the evil Lord Voldemort.

item.title: ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, over his claim that Nigeria could be wealthier if public funds were kept in banks to earn interest. Reacting in a post on his X account on Wednesday, Keyamo described Obi’s remarks as unintelligent and linked them to what he claimed was a decline in the former governor’s approval ratings. “This dumbness is beyond measure. I really don’t know whether to laugh or to cry. No wonder his approval ratings have plummeted so badly. “Nigeria did not just dodge a bullet; it ducked a massive howitzer!” Keyamo wrote. Vanguard had reported that Obi, speaking during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, argued that Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The post ‘Nigeria dodged a massive howitzer,’ Keyamo slams Obi over public funds comment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gombe @30: Yahaya seeks continuity ahead of 2027
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has called for continuity in governance, political unity and sustained investment in critical sectors as the state marks 30 years of creation, saying its future must transcend the ambitions of any individual or political party. Yahaya, reflecting on the state’s three-decade journey, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to celebrate past achievements and assess how statehood had translated into improved living conditions, expanded opportunities and inclusive development. The governor, whose second term ends in 2027, urged political leaders, traditional rulers, religious institutions, youths and other stakeholders to approach the forthcoming political transition with responsibility, peace and commitment to the collective interest of the state. Speaking against the backdrop of the anniversary theme, “Reflecting on our History, Consolidating Progress, and Charting the Future,” Yahaya said successive generations must understand the state’s history, preserve developmental gains and build institutions capable of outlasting individual administrations. He also highlighted achievements recorded under his administration in education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, industrialisation, electricity, environmental protection, public service reform and grassroots development. Gombe State was created on October 1, 1996, by the late General Sani Abacha following years of agitation for greater political representation, accelerated development and governance closer to the people. Yahaya expressed gratitude to Abacha and the state’s founding fathers and mothers, saying their contributions laid the foundation on which successive administrations had built. “Thirty years ago, a dream that our people had carried for generations finally became a reality. It was the recognition of a longstanding aspiration for greater representation, accelerated development, political inclusion and a stronger voice within the Nigerian federation,” he said. item.content:encoded: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has called for continuity in governance, political unity and sustained investment in critical sectors as the state marks 30 years of creation, saying its future must transcend the ambitions of any individual or political party. Yahaya, reflecting on the state’s three-decade journey, said the anniversary provided an opportunity to celebrate past achievements and assess how statehood had translated into improved living conditions, expanded opportunities and inclusive development. The governor, whose second term ends in 2027, urged political leaders, traditional rulers, religious institutions, youths and other stakeholders to approach the forthcoming political transition with responsibility, peace and commitment to the collective interest of the state. Speaking against the backdrop of the anniversary theme, “Reflecting on our History, Consolidating Progress, and Charting the Future,” Yahaya said successive generations must understand the state’s history, preserve developmental gains and build institutions capable of outlasting individual administrations. He also highlighted achievements recorded under his administration in education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, industrialisation, electricity, environmental protection, public service reform and grassroots development. Gombe State was created on October 1, 1996, by the late General Sani Abacha following years of agitation for greater political representation, accelerated development and governance closer to the people. Yahaya expressed gratitude to Abacha and the state’s founding fathers and mothers, saying their contributions laid the foundation on which successive administrations had built. “Thirty years ago, a dream that our people had carried for generations finally became a reality. It was the recognition of a longstanding aspiration for greater representation, accelerated development, political inclusion and a stronger voice within the Nigerian federation,” he said. He, however, noted that state creation alone did not guarantee development, stressing that its value lay in expanding opportunities, deepening inclusion, improving governance and enhancing citizens’ welfare. According to him, Gombe’s development cannot be credited to any single administration, political party or individual, describing governance as a relay in which each generation must advance the work of its predecessors. The governor paid tribute to the state’s pioneer military administrators, Group Captain Joseph Orji and Lieutenant Colonel Mohammed Inuwa Bawa, for establishing the machinery of government and laying the institutional foundations of the state. He also acknowledged the contributions of the late Alhaji Abubakar Habu Hashidu, the first democratically elected governor; Senator Mohammed Danjuma Goje; and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, whose administrations, he said, contributed to the expansion of infrastructure, institutions and development opportunities. Yahaya, who served as Commissioner for Finance and Economic Development under Goje, said successive administrations had operated under different circumstances but contributed to the state’s development. “When I took the oath of office on May 29, 2019, I made a simple commitment: to leave Gombe better than I found it,” he said. He said the commitment informed his administration’s 10-year development agenda, DEVAGOM, designed to promote people-centred governance through institutional reforms, strategic investments and inclusive development. Education: Over 2,000 classrooms constructed, renovated On education, Yahaya said his administration declared a state of emergency in the sector and embarked on extensive infrastructure development to improve access to quality learning. He disclosed that more than 2,000 classrooms had been constructed or renovated across more than 400 schools, while four mega colleges had been built and 1,000 teachers recruited. The administration also provided school improvement grants, while the Better Education Service Delivery for All programme, BESDA, was used to bring 350,000 out-of-school children back into the education system. He added that integrated Almajiri and Tsangaya schools had been established across the state’s 11 local government areas to expand access to education. At the tertiary level, Yahaya said two additional faculties had been established at Gombe State University, while increased subventions had strengthened tertiary institutions’ capacity to deliver teaching, research and innovation. He described the enactment of the Gombe State Education Trust Fund Law as a major step towards establishing a sustainable financing framework for the sector. According to him, education remains central to the state’s long-term prosperity, competitiveness and social development. Healthcare: GoHealth covers over 400,000 beneficiaries In the health sector, Yahaya said his administration had constructed or renovated 228 primary healthcare centres to provide two functional facilities in each of the state’s 114 political wards. He listed the construction of the General Hospital in Kumo, its subsequent conversion into a Federal Medical Centre, the renovation of general hospitals in Bajoga and Kaltungo, and the upgrading of the Gombe State Specialist Hospital among the interventions recorded under his administration. The governor said the establishment of the Hospitals Management Board was intended to improve healthcare administration, while the GoHealth contributory healthcare scheme had expanded access to medical services. According to him, the scheme now covers more than 400,000 beneficiaries, including approximately 100,000 poor and vulnerable citizens. He added that 440 healthcare professionals had been recruited and the CONMESS and CONHESS salary structures implemented to improve remuneration for health workers. Yahaya said the measures reflected his administration’s commitment to making healthcare more accessible, particularly to rural communities and vulnerable populations. Infrastructure, urban renewal and housing On infrastructure, the governor said the Network 11-100 initiative had facilitated the construction and rehabilitation of more than 1,000 kilometres of roads across the state, with several roads complemented by solar-powered streetlights. He listed the Gombe City Centre Underpass and the Gombe Northern Bypass among the major projects undertaken to improve mobility, connect communities, enhance public safety and stimulate economic activity. The administration, he said, also established the Gombe Geographic Information Systems (GOGIS) and reformed the Gombe State Urban Planning and Development Authority (GOSUPDA) to strengthen land administration, physical planning and urban development. Yahaya disclosed that work had commenced on a Three-Arms Zone comprising the State House of Assembly Complex, State High Court Complex and State Secretariat. He said the government had also constructed 550 housing units through the Family Homes Funds and another 500 in collaboration with the North-East Development Commission. According to him, the investments were intended to strengthen democratic institutions, improve public administration and provide housing opportunities for residents. Industrialisation, agriculture and investment In agriculture and industrialisation, Yahaya said the government was working to harness Gombe’s economic advantages by promoting productivity, value addition, enterprise development and private-sector investment. He identified the 1,000-hectare Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park as a major investment in the state’s industrial future, providing a platform for manufacturing, entrepreneurship and employment generation. The ongoing Renewed Hope Agro-Industrial Hub, he said, was designed to position Gombe as a major centre for agricultural trading, processing and logistics in the North-East. The fa

item.title: Judicial Reform: NBA’s unheeded proposal to restructure NJC
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri About two and a half years ago, precisely in April 2024, the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) proposed a bold reform to remove the Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, as the statutory chairman of the National Judicial Council, NJC. The NBA, as the umbrella body of legal practitioners in the country, faulted the composition of the Council, which is saddled with the responsibility of disciplining erring judicial officers. It not only challenged the current system, which mandates that the Council be headed by the CJN, but also demanded a review of its composition. According to the NBA: “The inherent flaws in the composition of the NJC impact negatively on its ability to prosecute judicial misconduct in a manner that inspires public confidence.” As part of its recommendations, the Bar proposed that the NJC be constituted as follows: six judicial officers appointed by the CJN; six lawyers nominated by the National Executive Council of the NBA, including the NBA President; and six non-lawyers appointed by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, subject to Senate approval. “The Chairmanship of these bodies should be rotated between the heads of the three constituent groups,” the NBA insisted. Furthermore, the association recommended appointing court administrators to assume the administrative functions currently performed by the heads of court, including procurement, budgeting, court renovation, and the implementation of judicial appropriations. “These are activities within court administration that have severally been identified by the anti-corruption bodies as areas prone to corrupt activities. “This proposal for the creation of this office takes cognizance of the role of the Chief Registrars of courts who will under the proposed arrangements enable them (together with heads of courts) to concentrate solely on the business of adjudication especially case management without distraction.” The recommendations were contained in proposals the NBA submitted at a national summit on Justice Sector reforms. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri About two and a half years ago, precisely in April 2024, the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) proposed a bold reform to remove the Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, as the statutory chairman of the National Judicial Council, NJC. The NBA, as the umbrella body of legal practitioners in the country, faulted the composition of the Council, which is saddled with the responsibility of disciplining erring judicial officers. It not only challenged the current system, which mandates that the Council be headed by the CJN, but also demanded a review of its composition. According to the NBA: “The inherent flaws in the composition of the NJC impact negatively on its ability to prosecute judicial misconduct in a manner that inspires public confidence.” As part of its recommendations, the Bar proposed that the NJC be constituted as follows: six judicial officers appointed by the CJN; six lawyers nominated by the National Executive Council of the NBA, including the NBA President; and six non-lawyers appointed by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, subject to Senate approval. “The Chairmanship of these bodies should be rotated between the heads of the three constituent groups,” the NBA insisted. Furthermore, the association recommended appointing court administrators to assume the administrative functions currently performed by the heads of court, including procurement, budgeting, court renovation, and the implementation of judicial appropriations. “These are activities within court administration that have severally been identified by the anti-corruption bodies as areas prone to corrupt activities. “This proposal for the creation of this office takes cognizance of the role of the Chief Registrars of courts who will under the proposed arrangements enable them (together with heads of courts) to concentrate solely on the business of adjudication especially case management without distraction.” The recommendations were contained in proposals the NBA submitted at a national summit on Justice Sector reforms. The Chairman of the Joint Planning Committee of the summit, Dr. Babatunde Ajibade, SAN, had, at that time, told newsmen that the reform proposals were considered and approved in modified form. “The general consensus reached by this panel was that the role of the NJC in discharging its responsibility for judicial appointments into the Superior Courts of Record required significant review. “There was a concern expressed about the fact that the CJN, who is the chairman of the NJC is also the chairman of the Federal Judicial Service Commission, which is the body that initially reviews proposals or lists of candidates for appointment into judicial office. “The members pointed out the seeming inconsistency between the CJN playing both those roles, as it would appear that he was then recommending candidates to himself being chairman of both bodies, and being the person who appoints a significant number of the members of both bodies other than those who are statutory members. “There was a general consensus that there was a need to reconstitute or propose the reconstitution of these bodies, both the NJC and the FJSC,” Ajibade, SAN, stated. However, years after the recommendations were made, both the NJC and the FJSC have remained structurally unchanged. The NJC was established under Section 153 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to safeguard the independence of the judiciary and ensure accountability in judicial administration. It was created as a replacement for the Advisory Judicial Committee (AJC), a legal body that operated during the military era, at a time when the judiciary had far less structural and administrative independence. With the return of the country to constitutional democracy, the NJC became the top judicial oversight organ, headed by the CJN, with its membership including the next most senior Justice of the Supreme Court; the President of the Court of Appeal; retired justices; various heads of courts; members of the NBA; and two non-lawyers of unquestionable integrity. Under the provisions of Paragraph 21 of Part One of the Third Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Council, among other things, recommends those to be appointed judges, as well as the removal from office of judicial officers found to have compromised standards in the discharge of their duties. The NJC makes such recommendations both to the President for judges under the Federal Judicial Service Commission (FJSC) and to Governors for judicial officers under the State Judicial Service Commissions. It is also the responsibility of the Council, through its committee, to periodically evaluate the performance of judges to ensure that the justice needs of citizens are duly met. Over the years, however, critics have called for a review of both the powers and composition of the NJC, citing its increasing failure to discharge its mandate effectively. A key area of concern is the judicial recruitment process, with critics arguing that unfit persons continue to be appointed, many of them either children of serving or retired judicial officers, or individuals loyal to people within the corridors of power. Critics insist that this has contributed to the poor quality of judicial decisions, often manifesting in conflicting judgments accompanied by allegations of bribery and corruption. The NJC is considered structurally weak: its members serve part-time, petitions are often decided at a snail’s pace, and sanctions feel token relative to the scale of corruption allegations. Notwithstanding the criticisms, the Council has periodically sacked or recommended the removal of judges for misconduct, and set up dedicated disciplinary machinery. In what appears to be the first major sweep to root out rotten eggs on the bench, the NJC, in a landmark resolution following its 111th meeting on May 13, 2026, queried 256 judges over various performance-related issues. It also suspended two High Court judges for one year without pay for misconduct and for breaching the right to a fair hearing. These developments followed renewed efforts by the CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, to cleanse the Augean stable. Justice Kekere-Ekun declared her zero tolerance for corruption when she appeared before the Senate for screening as the 23rd substantive CJN on September 25, 2024. True to her word, and in a clear departure from the old format, publication of the list of candidates shortlisted for appointment to the bench became mandatory. This paved the way for the public to blow the whistle on candidates with a deficit in their integrity quotient. Despite this initiative, calls for swifter action to guarantee accountability from the bench grew louder. It is not surprising that President Bola Tinubu had, in his 2023 manifesto, pledged to review the mandate and composition of the NJC. He said his administration would reposition the Council “to make it tougher and more effective in dealing with corruption, malpractice and incompetence in the administration of justice.” He had also proposed that the mandate of the NJC be limited to federal courts. However, more than three years into his administration, no changes have been made in either the composition or operations of the Council, even though President Tinubu himself has repeatedly acknowledged the need for reforms. He had, on November 17, 2025, urged the judiciary to take decisive action to address questions about its integrity, warning that justice must never be for sale. “Corruption in any arm of government weakens the nation, but corruption in the Judiciary destroys it at its core. “When justice is compromised, governance loses its integrity, and democracy loses its foundation,” President Tinubu stated as he flagged off the 2025 All Nigerian Judges Conference of the Superior Courts in Abuja. While acknowledging the concerns raised by President Tinubu, the CJN pledged action to restore public conf

item.title: Kalu opposes plenary invitation to INEC chairman
item.description: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has opposed a proposal to invite the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, to brief the House on preparations for the 2027 general elections, arguing that the engagement could distract the commission. Kalu made the position known during Wednesday’s plenary while contributing to a motion jointly sponsored by the Minority Whip, Mansur Soro, and the Deputy Minority Leader, Abdulsamad Dasuki, seeking to invite the INEC chairman to address lawmakers on the commission’s preparations for the elections. Opposing the prayer seeking a plenary briefing, the deputy speaker argued that INEC’s recent public engagements were sufficient to address many of the concerns raised about the electoral process. He said further inquiries should be channelled through the House Committee on Electoral Matters, which has the mandate to interface with the commission on behalf of the legislature. According to Kalu, inviting the INEC chairman before the full House at this stage could create unnecessary pressure on the commission, trigger public anxiety and undermine confidence in the electoral process. He maintained that the commission had been engaging the public on its preparations and had not reported any logistical challenges. “I stand not in support of the prayer of this particular motion because supporting the prayer is belittling the mandate of the committee set up to carry out this function,” he said. Kalu questioned the need to summon Amupitan before the entire House shortly after his public briefing, urging lawmakers to have confidence in the relevant committees established to oversee the commission’s activities. “Inviting the chairman of INEC to come and brief the House when he just briefed the entire nation is not ideal. Don’t we believe in our committees again?” he asked. He proposed an amendment to the motion to require the INEC chairman to meet with the relevant committee rather than address the entire House at plenary. The deputy speaker also argued that the National Assembly, as an institution responsible for strengthening democracy, should support the electoral commission in carrying out its responsibilities rather than subjecting it to what he considered an ill-timed plenary inquiry. His proposed amendment was seconded by a member of the House, Babajimi Benson, who represents a constituency in Lagos State. When the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, put the motion to a voice vote, lawmakers overwhelmingly supported the amendment, after which he referred the matter to the House Committee on Electoral Matters. The committee is expected to handle the concerns raised in the motion and engage with INEC on its preparations for the 2027 general elections. The post Kalu opposes plenary invitation to INEC chairman appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US bans imports from Chinese genomics companies
item.description: The United States banned imports from three Chinese genomics companies on Wednesday over claims they collected genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities in China’s Xinjiang region. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said BGI Genomics, MGI Tech and Shenzhen BGI Technology, also known as BGI Group, had been added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List. The list identifies entities working with Xinjiang’s government “to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor or receive forced labor or Uyghurs, Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, or members of other persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.” The United Nations warned in 2022 of possible crimes against humanity in the region, including the detention of more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in camps. China has repeatedly and vehemently denied accusations of human rights abuses against the Uyghurs. According to the US DHS, the companies “helped collect genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities, including people subjected to forced labor, meaning work they could not freely refuse.” Beijing said on Thursday that it “strongly condemns” Washington’s ban, which has “no factual basis”. “The US side continues to exploit the ‘human rights’ issue, using it as a pretext to pursue unilateral protectionism and bullying,” a commerce ministry spokesperson said in a statement. China urged the United States to “immediately cease its political manipulation and smear campaigns”, vowing to take necessary measures to safeguard its interests. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the United States refused to “let companies tied to forced labor and the surveillance of persecuted minorities profit from the American market.” BGI and MGI both denied the allegations, saying they oppose all forms of forced labour. The Trump administration proposed new rules last week to restrict investment in Chinese biotechnology companies. Other technologies already subject to scrutiny include artificial intelligence and computer chips — key frontiers in the ongoing economic competition between Beijing and Washington. AFP The post US bans imports from Chinese genomics companies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Football fan jailed for threats over Di Maria return to Argentina
item.description: An Argentine court jailed a football supporter for seven and a half years on Wednesday for threatening Angel Di Maria in 2024 in a bid to stop the World Cup winner returning to Argentina at the end of his career. A court in Rosario found Sergio Di Vanni, 45, guilty of ordering acts of intimidation against Di Maria’s family with the aim of dissuading the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for a rival club. Di Maria was playing for Benfica at the time, in March 2024, but was considering a return to his boyhood club Rosario Central, a move he eventually completed in 2025. Rosario Central and Newell’s Old Boys, Lionel Messi’s childhood club, are the two major teams in Rosario and fierce local rivals. The threats included gunshots fired near a gated community where Di Maria owns a property and the dumping of a pig’s head bearing a bullet wound outside an estate agency run by his sister, alongside a message threatening his daughter. A 25-year-old woman, Belen Gutierrez, identified by prosecutors as one of the perpetrators, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after entering a plea agreement. A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the two carried out the threats in exchange for four million pesos ($2,600). According to the prosecution, the intimidation campaign was linked to an internal power struggle among Newell’s ultras. Di Vanni’s sentence also covered separate offences related to his involvement in the supporters’ group. Following the threats, Di Maria initially abandoned plans to return to Argentina for the safety of his family. He ultimately reversed that decision and, now 38, has spent the past two seasons at Rosario Central, helping the club win the Argentine title at the end of 2025. item.title: US judge rejects Trump admin interference in California midterm vote
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday rejected the US Department of Justice’s efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens, slamming the move as brazen pre-election “interference.” The case sparked an uproar ahead of the November 3 midterms, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress, and appears to represent another attempt to cast doubt on electoral results. Democratic Party leaders have sued the Trump administration over the request, accusing Republicans of aiming “threats and intimidation” at state and local officials before the vote. US District Judge David O. Carter agreed, refusing to order the seizure of the ballots and siding with the government of Democratic-led California. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” Carter wrote in his decision. “Constitutional rights and our democracy are at stake. The public interest favors their protection,” he added. Those registered on California’s voter roles “must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors.” The federal government in recent months had accused California of having 190,000 illegal voters on its books. It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit about 10 days ago — after early voting had begun — to stop the state from sending ballots to them. A similar controversy arose in neighboring Nevada, where the allegations fizzled. The Trump administration had initially identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185 — and then to zero. “The DOJ’s actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials,” Carter wrote in his decision. For months, Trump — who has never acknowledged his own election defeat by Joe Biden in 2020 — has been claiming that there will be fraud in this year’s midterms. Studies repeatedly show that while rare cases of voter fraud exist, such incidents are miniscule and do not influence election results. AFP The post US judge rejects Trump admin interference in California midterm vote appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops kill 44 terrorists, scores injured in separate offensive in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 44 suspected members of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists during several offensive operations in some parts of Borno State. The encounter also left scores of terrorists injured, with destruction of their vehicles, motorcycles and Improvised Explosive Device (IED) materials. These were disclosed by the Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni in a press statement on Thursday morning. He said: “Troops of OPHK has sustained its offensive against terrorist elements through coordinated intelligence-led operations across the theatre. “On 26 October 2026, troops conducted engagements against suspected terrorist elements at separate locations in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State, following intelligence reports and surveillance observations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicated that 28 terrorists were neutralised, while six others reportedly sustained injuries. “In further operations on 28 October 2026, the Maritime Component, Naval Base Lake Chad deployed in Baga, conducted offensive actions against terrorist targets within the Lake Chad area. “Preliminary assessments indicated that eight terrorists were neutralised, while 10 others reportedly sustained varying degrees of injuries. “Separately, an air interdiction mission successfully disrupted a suspected terrorist improvised explosive device (IED)-laying operation, neutralising eight operatives and destroying their vehicle, motorcycles and IED materials. “The operation prevented the terrorist team from proceeding with its planned activity. “These successes reflect the sustained pressure being exerted on terrorist networks through intelligence-led joint operations,” Goni explained. He noted that OPHK remains committed to degrading terrorist capabilities, restricting their freedom of action and protecting communities across the North East. The Theatre Command urged members of the public to continue providing credible information to security agencies in support of ongoing efforts to restore lasting peace and security across the theatre. The post Troops kill 44 terrorists, scores injured in separate offensive in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Esther Christian: Orphaned at 4, bags scholarship as debate champion at 15
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has offered full scholarship up to university level to 15-year-old Esther Christian, the captain of the Abia debate team that emerged victorious at the 2026 International Schools Debate Championship in Doha, Qatar. Christian, who lost her father at the age of four, will enjoy the scholarship through the Alex Otti Foundation. Otti announced the gesture while hosting the victorious students at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, where he also awarded N1 million each to the five students who represented Abia State and Nigeria at the international competition. The governor further awarded N1 million to Onyinyechi Okonkwo of Ovom Girls Secondary School, winner of a recent national essay competition; N750,000 each to officials who accompanied the debate team; and N1.75 million to Abia Model Basic Junior Secondary School, Abayi Umuocham, Osisioma Ngwa, which produced the champions. Presenting trophies, medals and certificates to the students, Otti reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to transforming the state’s education sector through sustained investment, improved infrastructure and wider access to quality education. “This is in the DNA of Abia State. We celebrate people. When you do well, we celebrate you,” the governor said. He also approved the team’s request to participate in the 2027 edition of the competition, noting that although progress had been recorded in the education sector, more work remained to be done. Earlier, the Chairman of the Abia State Universal Basic Education Board (ASUBEB), Mrs Lydia Ezinne Onuoha, who led the team to Qatar, said the students did not merely participate in the competition but distinguished themselves among more than 84 teams. She said the team won four trophies and 12 medals after defeating representatives of six countries. According to her, the students clinched the Best International School Debate Team, Overall Best Team in the Junior Category, Best Debater and Best Leadership awards. They also ranked among the tournament’s top 10 speakers. Onuoha disclosed that during the five final rounds, contestants were given impromptu topics and just 15 minutes to prepare and present their arguments. The Coordinator of the President’s Schools Debate Championship, Elder Oritu Dare, said the victory had created an opportunity for Nigeria to participate in the next edition of the competition in Singapore. He also commended the governor for infrastructural development in the state. The Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Elder Goodluck Ubochi, said the achievements recorded in the education sector were only the beginning, expressing confidence that sustained investment would produce better results. Similarly, the Abia State Coordinator of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Mrs Unyime Umoette, said public schools were becoming more functional and urged public office holders to adopt schools in their communities and support their development.

item.title: Soaring duties, FX rates cripple Nigeria’s used-vehicle market
item.description: •As dealers lament sales slump By Glory Bassey Car dealers in Nigeria have lamented a sharp decline in vehicle sales, blaming soaring import duties, high exchange rate and rising cost of living as reasons why car ownership is increasingly becoming unaffordable for many Nigerians. A car dealer and importer, Mr Paul Uche, said the auto market segment has experienced a significant change in prices and customer patronage, with most vehicles now selling over five times higher than the prices three years ago. Uche said that a 2005 Toyota Corolla that previously sold for about N1.5 million now costs between N8 million and N8.5 million, depending on its condition and grade. Similarly, a Toyota Camry 2010 model that sold for between N2.2 million and N3 million now goes for N9 million to N10 million. He said the situation had worsened this year, with sales dropping considerably compared with previous years, adding: “you can even stay three to four months without making any sales; the situation is frustrating for people struggling to keep their businesses afloat. The impact is also evident in the market for locally used vehicles.” The dealer explained that a Nigerian-used 2005 Toyota Corolla, which previously sold for between N750, 000 and N850, 000, now costs between N4.3 million and N4.5 million, further limiting the number of prospective buyers able to afford a car. Identifying the exchange rate as one of the major factors driving the price increases, the dealer said the cost of importing vehicles has risen alongside customs duties and other clearing expenses. He recalled that clearing a Corolla previously cost between N200,000 and N350,000, but now requires between N2.5 million and N3.5 million. While saying that rising cost of clearing imported vehicles has placed additional pressure on dealers and customers, he pleaded with the government to review the situation, warning that the combination of high import costs and weak purchasing power was hurting the business. He also linked the decline in patronage to the rising cost of living, noting that higher rents, food prices and other household expenses had left many Nigerians struggling to meet basic needs. “You wouldn’t expect somebody who is struggling to survive to look at buying a car”. The post Soaring duties, FX rates cripple Nigeria’s used-vehicle market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Spain Begins Three-Day Mourning After Latest Train Tragedy Kills 68
item.description: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured scores, with relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones. One of Europe’s deadliest train disasters this century has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain’s rail network after the transport minister reported an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the crash. The collision happened in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo. Emergency services combed through the wreckage at night to find further victims on the key line linking Madrid with the southern city of Seville, hoisting pieces of mangled metal with cranes, AFP reporters saw. Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian who was holidaying in Spain with his girlfriend, said he was sleeping on the Renfe train when “I woke up and I was in the air.” Pablo Mejia, 42, escaped with injuries to his head, telling AFP that a last-minute change of seat saved his life. Wearing a bloodstained grey jumper and holding his tattered suitcase, he recounted “a very strong hit… a lot of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos”. “I think I’ve been born again,” he said. Members of the Parliament observe a minute of silence for the victims of a fatal train crash in Spain at the end of the state budget debate at the Portuguese parliament in Lisbon, on October 28, 2026. ‘Long And Hard Hours’ A school in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, is being used to allow relatives to enquire about their loved ones. Teams of Red Cross workers offered support to groups of people who arrived, some of them in tears, amid crowds of police and journalists from around the world. Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia said “long and hard hours” were in store because “every person will manage it in their own way. “We have people who are in shock, who haven’t taken on board what has happened, angry people, sad, worried people. The grieving will be complicated,” Garcia said. People arrive at a support center for relatives of missing victims in Urda, following the train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on October 28, 2026. The Civil Guard has set up four offices in the cities of Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to enable relatives of the victims to provide DNA samples and help identify the missing. Blood donation points have also been set up in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid. Teams of Red Cross workers offered support to groups of people who arrived, some of them in tears, amid crowds of police and journalists from around the world. Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia said “long and hard hours” were in store because “every person will manage it in their own way. “We have people who are in shock, who haven’t taken on board what has happened, angry people, sad, worried people. The grieving will be complicated,” Garcia said. People arrive at a support center for relatives of missing victims in Urda, following the train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on October 28, 2026. The Civil Guard has set up four offices in the cities of Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to enable relatives of the victims to provide DNA samples and help identify the missing. Blood donation points have also been set up in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid. Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined the emergency services in offering support to the victims’ families. “What matters most is being with the victims’ relatives, that they feel the closeness, because words at a time like this are pointless, but a hug helps,” he said. Recalling how he rushed to the site of the crash, Fernandez said he was confronted with “an image of desolation, despair, uncertainty, death”. Civil guards stand near victims at the site of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo, on October 28, 2026. Safety Questions Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system went down on 69 kilometres (43 miles) of track, causing all trains there to be stopped. But the control centre decided to “resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable,” Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25 kilometres before striking the Iryo. The control centre “had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it”, he added. In January, two high-speed trains collided in the southern region of Andalusia after one of them derailed and crossed onto the adjacent track, killing 46 people. The investigation into that accident is ongoing, but the left-wing government faced heavy criticism over its management of Spain’s railways. The latest disaster comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. item.title: Over 50% of financial industry ready for data localisation — CBN
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) yesterday said that more than 50 per cent of Nigeria’s financial industry is ready to comply with data localisation requirements, stressing that the country must strengthen its digital sovereignty without undermining innovation and global technology integration. The Director, Payment System Supervision Department, CBN, Dr. Rakyat Yusuf, disclosed this at the CBN-National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) Executive Regulatory Dialogue on the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative (NSCI) and data localisation in Lagos. Yusuf said a survey conducted by the apex bank showed that more than half of the industry was prepared to comply, expressing optimism that the remaining institutions would make progress following clarifications provided at the dialogue. “A survey we conducted to generate data on the level of preparedness has shown that more than 50 per cent of the industry is ready to comply,” she said. She added: “Ultimately, we expect everyone to be on board by January 2027 to ensure that payment data is properly localised.” According to her, the policy is about “our sovereignty, clarity and visibility over our transaction data,” as well as ensuring financial system stability.” Yusuf said the CBN’s priority was to support financial institutions in achieving compliance rather than resorting immediately to sanctions. “However, where we identify a deliberate attempt to avoid compliance, sanctions will come into play. There will be sanctions for non-compliance,” she warned. Also speaking, the Deputy Governor, Financial System Stability, CBN, Lamido Yuguda, said Nigeria must strengthen control over its critical digital infrastructure while remaining open to global technological developments. He said: “The objective of the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative should not be to constrain innovation or isolate Nigeria from global technological developments. Rather, it should provide the security, resilience, and regulatory certainty necessary to support investment, innovation, and sustainable growth.” Yuguda said the resilience of the financial system increasingly depended on the digital infrastructure supporting it. He added: “We must strengthen digital sovereignty while remaining globally competitive; enhance security without constraining innovation; and promote localisation while ensuring that the financial system continues to benefit from efficient and reliable technology.” Meanwhile, NITDA Director-General, Kashifu Abdullahi, assured financial institutions that Nigeria’s technology ecosystem had the capacity to support the implementation of the sovereign cloud initiative. “Today’s workshop is to give you the assurance that the technology exists, the Nigerian tech ecosystem is capable, and it can support you in complying with your regulator’s mandate or directive,” he said. She added: “Ultimately, we expect everyone to be on board by January 2027 to ensure that payment data is properly localised.” According to her, the policy is about “our sovereignty, clarity and visibility over our transaction data,” as well as ensuring financial system stability.” Yusuf said the CBN’s priority was to support financial institutions in achieving compliance rather than resorting immediately to sanctions. “However, where we identify a deliberate attempt to avoid compliance, sanctions will come into play. There will be sanctions for non-compliance,” she warned. Also speaking, the Deputy Governor, Financial System Stability, CBN, Lamido Yuguda, said Nigeria must strengthen control over its critical digital infrastructure while remaining open to global technological developments. He said: “The objective of the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative should not be to constrain innovation or isolate Nigeria from global technological developments. Rather, it should provide the security, resilience, and regulatory certainty necessary to support investment, innovation, and sustainable growth.” Yuguda said the resilience of the financial system increasingly depended on the digital infrastructure supporting it. He added: “We must strengthen digital sovereignty while remaining globally competitive; enhance security without constraining innovation; and promote localisation while ensuring that the financial system continues to benefit from efficient and reliable technology.” Meanwhile, NITDA Director-General, Kashifu Abdullahi, assured financial institutions that Nigeria’s technology ecosystem had the capacity to support the implementation of the sovereign cloud initiative. “Today’s workshop is to give you the assurance that the technology exists, the Nigerian tech ecosystem is capable, and it can support you in complying with your regulator’s mandate or directive,” he said. Abdullahi said digital sovereignty was not about isolation or building every technology locally, but developing Nigeria’s capacity to compete globally and maintain control over critical infrastructure. “It is about building our digital capacity to compete in the world we are in today,” he said. He warned that external disruptions, including submarine cable outages and geopolitical crises, should not automatically affect Nigeria’s payment system. Abdullahi added that the initiative would provide financial institutions with greater choice of technology providers and help prevent dependence on a single vendor, country or technology platform. item.title: Hardship: Our problems with FG’s 90-day relief plan —Labour
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young In an apparent response to growing public concern and outcry over the high cost of living and the worsening economic hardship confronting Nigerians, the Federal Government recently announced a 90-day relief plan aimed at providing succour to workers and the wider population. However, rather than inspire confidence, the initiative has come under intense scrutiny from the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, which questions its transparency, effectiveness and capacity to address the underlying causes of the crisis. The labour centre has described the intervention as a “confession, not a solution,” arguing that temporary palliatives cannot replace concrete measures to tackle rising living costs, declining purchasing power and widespread impoverishment. The NLC also demanded the disclosure of the details of the plan, alongside concrete action on wage awards, petroleum prices, tax relief and the review of the national minimum wage, arguing that Nigerians need practical solutions rather than another set of promises. In this interview with Vanguard, NLC Assistant General Secretary, Chris Onyeka, explains the labour movement’s reservations about the plan, outlines its demands for urgent economic relief and challenges the Federal Government to move beyond promises and implement sustainable solutions to the hardship facing Nigerian workers and the masses. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Victor Ahiuma-Young In an apparent response to growing public concern and outcry over the high cost of living and the worsening economic hardship confronting Nigerians, the Federal Government recently announced a 90-day relief plan aimed at providing succour to workers and the wider population. However, rather than inspire confidence, the initiative has come under intense scrutiny from the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, which questions its transparency, effectiveness and capacity to address the underlying causes of the crisis. The labour centre has described the intervention as a “confession, not a solution,” arguing that temporary palliatives cannot replace concrete measures to tackle rising living costs, declining purchasing power and widespread impoverishment. The NLC also demanded the disclosure of the details of the plan, alongside concrete action on wage awards, petroleum prices, tax relief and the review of the national minimum wage, arguing that Nigerians need practical solutions rather than another set of promises. In this interview with Vanguard, NLC Assistant General Secretary, Chris Onyeka, explains the labour movement’s reservations about the plan, outlines its demands for urgent economic relief and challenges the Federal Government to move beyond promises and implement sustainable solutions to the hardship facing Nigerian workers and the masses. Onyeka said: “Our response to the federal government’s so-called 90-day plan to ease the cost of living is unambiguous. This plan is not a remedy; it is a confession. It is the government’s tacit admission, finally dragged out of it by the sheer weight of popular suffering, that its policies of the past nearly four years have afflicted the Nigerian people rather than improved their lives. “For years, the government denied that its reforms were producing pain. Various Ministers told us there was no suffering while other official spokespeople insisted the economy was on the right track. Now, with the announcement of a 90-day cost-of-living plan, the government has conceded the obvious; something is deeply wrong, and it was caused by the very policies it once defended. “But a confession is not a cure and, a plan cobbled together in panic is not a plan for the people. It is perceptibly playing politics with the genuine cries of Nigerian workers and masses. ‘We haven’t seen the plan’ “The truth is that we have not seen the Plan neither have any citizen It claims to help. We know that the most basic demand of any democratic governance is transparency. Yet nobody; not us in the NLC, not civil society, not the Nigerian workers and masses facing the crisis of survival daily; has seen this 90-day plan or knows what it contains. Any genuine plan to reduce the suffering of Nigerian workers would be a welcome development. But it is our responsibility, as the organised voice of workers, to demand that the government put this plan on the table for all of us to see. “Have we not been here before? Just a few weeks ago, the federal government came up with a 30-day selected fuel discount that was clearly a panic measure that amounted to nothing. It did not work in any way to assuage the sufferings of the people as it was tokenism dressed up as policy. “We would have loved to have been hopeful but we regrettably have no reason to believe the 90-day plan is anything more than a repeat performance; another promise on paper designed to hoodwink Nigerian workers and masses, just like the schemes and promises that came before it. “In generating this plan, Government should be bold to tell Nigerians who it Consulted? That is the question the Government may not be able to answer. We must also ask; which stakeholders did the government consult before coming up with such a plan? Did it consult the trade union movement; the organised representatives of Nigerian workers? Did it consult the civil society organisations that represent the people it governs? “There is no workable solution that can proceed from a government whose policy measures of the last nearly four years have only caused humongous hardship among the citizenry. Effective and sustainable solutions can only be founded when government learns to engage the people in creative conversations. It is not when you sit down in the corridors of power and hand down schemes to the people, instead of allowing them to conceive, design and implement the projects and policies directed toward solving their own socioeconomic problems. “This top-down, elitist approach; the politics of imposition; is precisely why the policies fail. The people are treated as objects of policy rather than subjects of their own liberation. The 90 days are questionable days, designed once again to hoodwink Nigerian workers and masses for political gains. A palliative, not a solution “And we must ask the obvious question: even if whatever measures involved in the 90-day plan work, what happens to the people and workers after 90 days? A 90-day palliative is not a structural solution. It is a bandage on a wound that requires surgery. “The timing of this plan is deeply suspect; it reeks of political motivation, coming as it does ahead of the 2027 general elections cycle that begins in January 2027. This is not economic policy; it is electoral calculation dressed in the language of relief. “When we are therefore asked whether it does assuage our anger as NLC, we are compelled to retort that this is a question that misses the point. It is not right to talk about “NLC’s anger” because it never was. It is rather right to talk about the sufferings of Nigerian workers and masses so, the better question is: does this plan address the worries of the Nigerian people? It clearly does not as there are no signs on the ground since the pronouncement of the plans to demonstrate any serious implementation. “The NLC was never asking for tokenistic measures. We were asking for concrete actions that would ameliorate these sufferings. The situation clearly transcends feelings of anger; it is about the existential threats that confront every Nigerian daily as a result of the policies of government. “The government’s plan does not address these threats to the lives of Nigerian workers because there is no concrete and workable action around the so-called plan. Anger is a luxury of the comfortable; what Nigerian workers face is survival, and the government is offering them theatre. “Whether it meets our expectations deserves a very simple answer; No, because the basics are missing. The expectation of Nigerian workers and masses, as championed by the NLC, is that the yoke of hunger and impoverishment be lifted from off the shoulders of Nigerian workers and peoples. What we have received instead are just the usual promissory notes. “Specifically, where is the wage award to keep Nigerian workers and masses surviving until the next national minimum wage is implemented? Where is the reduction in the prices of petroleum products that would ease the cost of transportation around the country, thus reducing food inflation and the prices of other basic commodities? These are not radical demands; they are the minimum conditions for survival. The plan does not in any way meet our expectations as workers and as a people. “On whether it meets the demands of the NLC, it can be said that the Government decided to go fishing instead of embarking on providing clear-cut solutions. The so-called plan does not address the issue of kick-starting the process for a statutory review of the national minimum wage. “It does not speak to the demands of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC. “It does not speak to tax relief for Nigerian workers and masses, which would help put more money in the pockets of Nigerian workers. Government is therefore fishing and not seriously interested in solving the problems raised by the NLC. “This is governance by gesture; a politics of

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 29, 2026
item.description: Trading in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market opened on Thursday with the local currency displaying steady conditions against the United States dollar across both official and unofficial channels. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the Naira traded around N1,346.05 per US dollar. Spot market activity recorded moderate intra-day movements as commercial banks and corporate entities executed transactions for foreign trade, import bills, and capital remittances. The rate maintains a tight range following ongoing liquidity support and market interventions from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) aimed at easing demand pressure. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators in major hubs including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates floated near N1,385 per dollar. The parallel market premium remains relatively narrow compared to the official rate. Market analysts attribute the market stability to sustained external reserves, which hold above $55 billion. Strong foreign inflows from oil exports and diaspora remittances continue to support liquidity across both FX channels. Market participants expect trading conditions to remain stable as regular commercial order flows are absorbed throughout the business day. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 29, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 84.9m informal workers face retirement without safety net
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The National Pension Commission, PenCom, is stepping up efforts to expand pension coverage among Nigeria’s self-employed and informal sector workers, as an estimated 84.9 million people remain without pension coverage, exposing a significant gap in the country’s retirement security system. Figures presented at the 2026 Annual PenCom Media Conference in in Lagos, showed that although the informal sector accounts for an estimated 93 per cent of Nigeria’s workforce, only 242,690 informal sector workers had enrolled in the Personal Pension Plan, PPP, as of July 2026. The figures, based on estimates of the informal sector workforce, put pension coverage among the group at just 0.29 per cent, highlighting the challenge facing efforts to bring millions of traders, artisans, farmers, professionals and gig workers into the pension system. The Personal Pension Plan was introduced under Section 2(3) of the Pension Reform Act, PRA, 2014 to extend pension coverage to self-employed persons and workers in the informal sector who may not have access to conventional employer-sponsored retirement savings arrangements. The scheme allows eligible contributors to make flexible payments daily, weekly, monthly or at their convenience, depending on their income and circumstances. Registration requires a National Identification Number (NIN) and a phone number, while prospective contributors can register directly with a Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) or through an accredited pension agent. However, the presentation identified several obstacles to wider participation, including irregular earnings, limited awareness, distrust of financial institutions, preference for readily accessible savings, geographical barriers and gaps in digital literacy. For many informal sector workers, whose earnings may fluctuate considerably, setting aside money for retirement can be difficult when contributions compete with immediate household and business expenses The presentation also noted that access to a pension account does not necessarily translate into sustained savings, as some contributors may register without making regular or subsequent payments. It stressed that the success of the Personal Pension Plan should therefore be measured not only by the number of registered accounts but also by active contributors, frequency of contributions, consistency of saving, average account balances and the adequacy of retirement benefits. Under the Plan’s contribution structure, 50 per cent of contributions constitutes the contingent portion, which may be withdrawn three months after the initial contribution and subsequently once every two months. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The National Pension Commission, PenCom, is stepping up efforts to expand pension coverage among Nigeria’s self-employed and informal sector workers, as an estimated 84.9 million people remain without pension coverage, exposing a significant gap in the country’s retirement security system. Figures presented at the 2026 Annual PenCom Media Conference in in Lagos, showed that although the informal sector accounts for an estimated 93 per cent of Nigeria’s workforce, only 242,690 informal sector workers had enrolled in the Personal Pension Plan, PPP, as of July 2026. The figures, based on estimates of the informal sector workforce, put pension coverage among the group at just 0.29 per cent, highlighting the challenge facing efforts to bring millions of traders, artisans, farmers, professionals and gig workers into the pension system. The Personal Pension Plan was introduced under Section 2(3) of the Pension Reform Act, PRA, 2014 to extend pension coverage to self-employed persons and workers in the informal sector who may not have access to conventional employer-sponsored retirement savings arrangements. The scheme allows eligible contributors to make flexible payments daily, weekly, monthly or at their convenience, depending on their income and circumstances. Registration requires a National Identification Number (NIN) and a phone number, while prospective contributors can register directly with a Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) or through an accredited pension agent. However, the presentation identified several obstacles to wider participation, including irregular earnings, limited awareness, distrust of financial institutions, preference for readily accessible savings, geographical barriers and gaps in digital literacy. For many informal sector workers, whose earnings may fluctuate considerably, setting aside money for retirement can be difficult when contributions compete with immediate household and business expenses The presentation also noted that access to a pension account does not necessarily translate into sustained savings, as some contributors may register without making regular or subsequent payments. It stressed that the success of the Personal Pension Plan should therefore be measured not only by the number of registered accounts but also by active contributors, frequency of contributions, consistency of saving, average account balances and the adequacy of retirement benefits. Under the Plan’s contribution structure, 50 per cent of contributions constitutes the contingent portion, which may be withdrawn three months after the initial contribution and subsequently once every two months. The remaining 50 per cent is designated for retirement benefits and is accessible from age 50, or earlier in cases of medical incapacitation, subject to applicable regulations To widen participation, PenCom has accredited pension agents to help bring the scheme closer to underserved communities and workers who may have limited access to conventional pension services. The agents are expected to facilitate enrolment, support contributions and account updates through approved channels, and conduct public sensitisation and financial literacy activities. Six approved pension agents were listed in the presentation as having received accreditation across three dates in 2026: Awabah Remit Services Limited in February; e-Tranzact International Limited and NextAutomate APA Limited in June; and SunTrust Bank Nigeria Limited, PrimeTrust APA Limited and Majestic APA Limited in September. The presentation further identified financial literacy, trust-building, convenient payment channels and contribution arrangements suited to irregular earnings as important areas for improving participation and encouraging long-term saving. It also highlighted the gender dimension of the challenge, citing an estimate that 96 per cent of employed women work in the informal sector, making the expansion of pension coverage particularly relevant to women whose livelihoods fall outside formal employment arrangements. Beyond increasing enrolment, the commission’s challenge is to ensure that workers remain active contributors and accumulate sufficient savings to support them in retirement. The presentation concluded that expanding access alone would not close Nigeria’s pension gap. Sustained participation, consistent contributions and adequate retirement balances are essential to turning the Personal Pension Plan into a meaningful source of financial security for the country’s vast informal workforce. The post 84.9m informal workers face retirement without safety net appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon looks like a diamond in the rough
item.description: Just two weeks after launching Gemini 4 Argon, Google has announced a better-performing version of the model that it will sell for the same price, at least temporarily. Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, said Gemini 4 Carbon represents the company's strongest model yet, particularly in terms of cybersecurity and long-running tasks. There's some irony in the name "Carbon", given the Chocolate Factory plans a carbon-dioxide-free future . Given Google's political timidity when it comes to names on maps , Gemini 4 Americium might be more representative of management's worldview. Gemini 4 Silicon is another missed opportunity — the chemical symbol is Si, a bobbleheaded nod to "Super Intelligence." Priced initially at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, Gemini 4 Carbon sells for the same amount as its predecessor Argon during an indeterminate introductory period. When that period expires, Google will lift prices to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. That's the same as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, which Google clearly sees as Carbon's competition. Last month, Google's ability to compete in the wake of the leadership change at its DeepMind AI subsidiary looked less certain . But Carbon has posted impressive benchmark scores, taking the lead in SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym, and CWE-bench, while landing at fourth place on WebDev Arena , behind Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Astra, and Sonnet 5.5. Carbon currently ranks second, behind Opus 5.5, in Arena.ai's leaderboard for Best Overall Agent. Model ratings biz Artificial Analysis says Google's new model tops its newly formulated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and comes in second to Claude Code Opus 5.5 on its Coding Agent Index. Kavukcuoglu emphasized Carbon's cybersecurity capabilities, which will be available this week to an unspecified set of cybersecurity defenders and more eventually through the company's Fairwind access program. "On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon," he wrote. "As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10x better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches." "Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier," said Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, in a statement [PDF] accompanying Alphabet's Q3 2026 earnings. "Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago." While Google may hope to surpass Anthropic and OpenAI in terms of model performance and usage, it's already ahead in revenue. item.title: Boffin's software found a possible dwarf planet - a result so rare he thought it must be a bug
item.description: A scientist working on data gathered by the Rubin Observatory has found a strong candidate for our solar system’s sixth known dwarf planet. The Observatory is run by the USA’s National Science Foundation and Department of Energy, who built it on a remote hilltop in Chile and equipped it with the 3200-megapixel Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Camera, which came online in June 2026. As explained in a Tuesday announcement , Rubin Operations team member and project contributor Matthew Holman, of the Center for Astrophysics (CfA) at Harvard & Smithsonian, used search code he developed with CfA colleague Kevin Napier to analyze data captured before LSST operations commenced. The Observatory says Holman’s and Napier’s code “is built to look at billions of detections of moving objects, compare them, and find the detections that correspond to the same object.” On October 13, the code spotted an object so bright and distant that it is likely unusually large. “My first reaction was one of excited disbelief,” Holman said. “Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong.” Other astroboffins sprang into action, dug into other records, and soon found ten years’ worth of relevant data. Once they all checked their sums, the Minor Planet Center reviewed their work and announced the discovery of the romantically named 2026 ED138 and published lots of data about its orbit, which is at around 46 astronomical units (au). A single au is the distance from Earth to the Sun, and Pluto’s orbit averages 40 au. Rubin Observatory revealed its part in the effort and declared that 2026 ED138 is a good candidate for certification as a dwarf planet. The 2026 International Astronomical Union defines a dwarf planet as “an object in orbit around the Sun that is large enough to pull itself into a nearly round shape but has not been able to clear its orbit of debris.” The Union’s definition of a full planet includes having “an important influence on the orbital stability of the other objects in its neighbourhood.” Dwarf planets whirl about the solar system in relatively close company with many rocky and/or icy objects that orbit under the influence of other bodies, not the nearby dwarf planet. Rubin boffins think ED138 is between 600 and 1500 kilometers across. If the lower number is correct, it’s the smallest dwarf planet yet observed. Should the larger number be correct, it would be smaller than Pluto, Eris, and Haumea, but larger than Makemake and Ceres. Scientists at the observatory think ED138 has evaded detection to date because it was found in a region of sky close to the plane of the Milky Way — meaning observers had to pick it out from light cast by billions of stars. “Rubin Observatory’s regular and continuous monitoring of the entire Southern Hemisphere sky, combined with powerful algorithms that sift through millions to billions of points of light to identify those corresponding to small moving objec
item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: A scientist working on data gathered by the Rubin Observatory has found a strong candidate for our solar system’s sixth known dwarf planet. The Observatory is run by the USA’s National Science Foundation and Department of Energy, who built it on a remote hilltop in Chile and equipped it with the 3200-megapixel Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Camera, which came online in June 2026. As explained in a Tuesday announcement , Rubin Operations team member and project contributor Matthew Holman, of the Center for Astrophysics (CfA) at Harvard & Smithsonian, used search code he developed with CfA colleague Kevin Napier to analyze data captured before LSST operations commenced. The Observatory says Holman’s and Napier’s code “is built to look at billions of detections of moving objects, compare them, and find the detections that correspond to the same object.” On October 13, the code spotted an object so bright and distant that it is likely unusually large. “My first reaction was one of excited disbelief,” Holman said. “Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong.” Other astroboffins sprang into action, dug into other records, and soon found ten years’ worth of relevant data. Once they all checked their sums, the Minor Planet Center reviewed their work and announced the discovery of the romantically named 2026 ED138 and published lots of data about its orbit, which is at around 46 astronomical units (au). A single au is the distance from Earth to the Sun, and Pluto’s orbit averages 40 au. Rubin Observatory revealed its part in the effort and declared that 2026 ED138 is a good candidate for certification as a dwarf planet. The 2026 International Astronomical Union defines a dwarf planet as “an object in orbit around the Sun that is large enough to pull itself into a nearly round shape but has not been able to clear its orbit of debris.” The Union’s definition of a full planet includes having “an important influence on the orbital stability of the other objects in its neighbourhood.” Dwarf planets whirl about the solar system in relatively close company with many rocky and/or icy objects that orbit under the influence of other bodies, not the nearby dwarf planet. Rubin boffins think ED138 is between 600 and 1500 kilometers across. If the lower number is correct, it’s the smallest dwarf planet yet observed. Should the larger number be correct, it would be smaller than Pluto, Eris, and Haumea, but larger than Makemake and Ceres. Scientists at the observatory think ED138 has evaded detection to date because it was found in a region of sky close to the plane of the Milky Way — meaning observers had to pick it out from light cast by billions of stars. “Rubin Observatory’s regular and continuous monitoring of the entire Southern Hemisphere sky, combined with powerful algorithms that sift through millions to billions of points of light to identify those corresponding to small moving objects, enabled the team to spot ED138 within the crowded field,” the facility boasted. ®
